question: I have resigned from Indian oil Corporation 3 months ago back through proper channels and joined Odisha state government job in group A services. Now I want to go back to the previous psu job. Is it possible ?( Rourkela, Orissa )
answer: Dear Client,As per the Ministry of Finance Office Memo No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June 1965, the resignation is treated as a technical resignation where a Government servant has applied through proper channels for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met, even if the Government servant has not mentioned the word âTechnicalâ while submitting his resignation. The benefit of past service, if otherwise admissible under rules, may be given in such cases. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation and the benefit of past service will not be admissible. The benefit of past service is allowed in such cases subject to the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government servant should intimate the details of such application immediately on their joining; (ii) the Government servant at the time of resignation should specifically make a request, indicating that he is resigning to take up another appointment under the Government for which he applied before joining the Government service; (iii) the authority accepting the resignation should satisfy itself that had the employee been in service on the date of application for the post mentioned by the employee, his application would have been forwarded through proper channel. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within 2 years or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. Being the position as stated above you may seek further clarification on the subject from the concerned Deptt (DOPT) or apply to the State Administrative Tribunal (SAT) constituted under the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1985. But before approaching SAT, you have to represent your grievance before the HOD concerned and if your grievance is not resolved or you are aggrieved with the reply of the HOD to your grievance, you can apply before the concerned Bench of the State Administrative Tribunal(SAT) following the procedure as prescribed under the State Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules. If required, you may hire an advocate to handle SAT matters and navigate the issue in the right way.

The eligibility for an appointment under the Scheme for Compassionate Appointment was updated on 02/08/2022 by the Deptt. of Personnel and Training(DOPT), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievance and Pension, Govt. of India wherein scope and eligibility for employment under the compassionate appointment scheme are explained in detail. The Supreme Courtâs judgment dated May 4, 1994 in the case of Umesh Kumar Nagpal vs. State of Haryana and others [JT 1994(3) S.C. 525] has ruled that offering compassionate appointment as a matter of course irrespective of the financial condition of the family of the deceased or medically retired Government servant is legally impermissible. Compassionate appointment cannot be granted after a lapse of a reasonable period and it is not a vested right that can be exercised at any time in the future. The Supreme Court has also held in its judgment dated February 28, 1995 in the case of the Life Insurance Corporation of India vs. Mrs Asha Ramchandra Ambekar and others [JT 1994(2) S.C. 183] that the High Courts and Administrative Tribunals can not give direction for appointment of a person on compassionate grounds but can merely direct consideration of the claim for such an appointment. question: Legality of Serving Notice Period & Paying Bond Simultaneously.I signed a 2.3-year employment bond with my company, which requires me to pay â¹1,20,000 if I resign early. answer: Dear Client,A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compel the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret, then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, Further, SAMADHAN Portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to facilitate the filing of industrial disputes by the workmen, employers and trade unions under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The online portal has a user-friendly interface and has enhanced transparency and efficiency of grievance resolution for all stakeholders. The workmen/trade unions/management can file their disputes and claims by logging into the portal through the UMANG app and also by visiting the nearest Common Services Centres. But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947.

question: In July 2024, my previous employer paid me a Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) for the year 2023-2024. question:
I have for company A 1.5years and leave it on Mar 19,2022 and joined company B on Mar21,2022 now my doe of previous company is overlapping on doj my current company by approx 3months.
Now what I'm suppose do do to transfer my epf balance?( Jamshedpur, Jharkhand )
answer: Dear Client,Before joining another Company, you are required to tender your resignation and to obtain a relieving letter from the earlier company serving the notice period as per the terms of employment that eventually caused the overlapping of service. The overlapping in service concerning previous and present establishments and any anomaly or discrepancy in EPF records of any registered member may be grounds for future disputes. When your EPF record shows an anomaly in the joining and exit date in both the previous and present Company, which is contradictory, then until and unless those anomalies are rectified by the concerned employers, PF records will show overlapping or dual employment. A joint declaration form is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. An employee cannot update the service history. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database, he should contact their present or previous employers and get it corrected. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of dual employment/overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly/discrepancy arising out of date of appointment and date of exit of an employee in EPF records. For lack of cooperation from the employers who are duty-bound to correct the records of member employees in EPF records, an individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (https://epfigms.gov.in/) or file a complaint offline in the office of the Regional PF Commissioner concerned. If the complaint is not resolved even on receipt of JDF, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief is yielded from the office of the PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief. However, recently, EPFO has taken a resolution to waive the consent of an ex-employer for transferring a member's EPF Account to a new employer, which is yet to be notified.

question:
Is a remote employee in IT industry covered under Employeeâs Compensation Act, 1923 ? 
While working in the home office , If an employee fells accidently while plugging up the charger and gets back injury for which doctor  suggests for 4-5 weeks bed rest. Will this case be covered under Employeeâs Compensation Act, 1923 ?( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,A good query, especially in the increasing trend of virtual/digital modes of working followed by establishments/organisations across the country post-COVID-19. In India, the Government has yet to introduce any labour laws or guidelines around remote working. The doctrine of notional extension is a legal concept that expands the scope of employment beyond the traditional confines of a workplace. This theory prescribes that workers should receive compensation for accidents occurring during the course of employment, even if the incident takes place outside the physical work premises or regular working hours. The doctrine recognizes that employment-related risks can extend beyond the immediate work environment. To apply the doctrine of notional extension, three essential elements must be complied with 1) An accident, 2) Personal injury to the employee, 3) The injury must arise out of and occur during the course of employment. The phrase âarising out of employmentâ implies that there must be a causal connection between the injury and the duties or conditions of the work performed. This reflects the inherent risks associated with the job. Courts have interpreted these elements broadly, often extending the employerâs liability to include incidents during commutes or work-related travel. While the doctrine of notional extension aims to protect workers, it also incorporates exceptions to maintain balance. These exceptions include cases of short-term disabilities, employee intoxication, willful disobedience of safety orders, and incidents in public areas not directly related to employment duties. The doctrine of notional extension finds its legal foundation in the Workmenâs Compensation Act of 1923, now known as the Employeesâ Compensation Act. This doctrine extends the scope of an employerâs liability beyond the physical confines of the workplace, recognizing that employment doesnât necessarily begin and end at the office door. Section 3(1) of the Act forms the cornerstone of the doctrine of notional extension. It states that employers are liable to pay compensation if an employee suffers a personal injury due to an accident arising out of and in the course of employment. This provision has been interpreted broadly by Indian courts to include accidents that occur outside the workplace but are still connected to the employeeâs work duties. The Indian Government has recognised the doctrine of notional extension through its Employees Compensation Act, 1923. The Indian legal system recognizes that accidents occurring outside the workplace or working hours may still be related to employment. This interpretation has led to a more comprehensive protection for workers, extending liability to employers for incidents that might occur during commutes or in areas adjacent to the workplace. Courts have generally interpreted the doctrine liberally to provide compensation benefits to workers and their dependents, considering their social and economic conditions. Landmark cases like R.B. Moondra And Co. vs Mst. Bhanwari and Anr. have helped shape its interpretation. Given the scope of application of the doctrine of notional extension, you can approach your Company for compensation under the Employees Compensation Act, 1923.

question: Can someone tell me if the daughter in law can be given employment under the R&R policy 2012 of the coal india( Chandrapur, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,The main purpose of the Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy of Coal India Ltd is to provide adequate compensation to the people/families whose land was acquired for mining projects. Clause 11 of the R & R Policy defines Project Affected Family (PAF). âAffected familyâ and âFamilyâ that include a person, his or her spouse, minor sons, unmarried daughters, minor brothers, unmarried sisters, father, mother and other relatives residing with him or her and dependent on him or her for their livelihood; and includes ânuclear familyâ consisting of a person, his or her spouse and minor children.  This benefit shall accrue only to the Entitled Project Affected Person. Entitled Project Affected Person shall be one of the following categories. (i) Persons from whom land is acquired including tribals cultivating land under traditional rights. (ii) Persons whose homestead is acquired (iii), Sharecroppers, land lessees, tenants & day laborers. (iv) Tribal dependent on forest produce. All landowners with titles will receive monetary compensation for the land acquired from them. The value of the land is determined based on prevailing legal norms. Subject to suitability and availability of vacancies and further subject to the approval of the Board of Directors of the subsidiary company concerned, coal companies shall offer employment at the rate of one employment for every two acres of land acquired. Actual land losers or their dependants as prescribed in the R.R.Policy notified by the Ministry of Rural Development (MORD)shall either take employment or cash compensation as prescribed. In case there is no policy of the State Government for monetary compensation/financial package in lieu of employment against the land, the monetary compensation shall be paid on the following basis: i) Rs.200000/-(two lakhs) only for the first acre of land, on pro-rata basis subject to a minimum Rs.50000/-only. ii) Rs.150000/- (One and a half lakhs) only on a pro-rata basis for 2nd and 3rd acre of land. iii) Rs.100000/- (one lakh) only on a pro-rata basis for land beyond 3 acres. A person receiving a job forgoes all claims to the abovecompensation and a person receiving the above compensation forgoes all claims to employment. Special attempts are made to ensure that women will be given adequate access to income-generating opportunities offered under this policy. Clause 27 of the Policy laid down the Mechanism for dealing with disputes. According to this clause, a committee comprising nominee(s) of the State Government, nominee(s) of the project general manager of the subsidiaries, a representative of the Project Affected Person (PAP) and an independent party, such as a respected community leader, a retired judge or principal of a reputed local institution of higher education, will be constituted to examine the grievances of the PAP and propose corrective actions as required. So, you can seek the desired information from the said committee or and escalate your grievance before the said Committee for redressal of your grievance.

question: A woman named Sagorika humiliated me after I requested her to refrain from contacting me on WhatsApp outside of office hours. Despite my clear communication, she continued to message me. When I reiterated my request, she responded with derogatory language, using abusive words and asking how dare I instruct her. I would like to know the legal steps I can take against her for her unacceptable behavior.( Kolkata, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,Since there is no law or legislation protecting a man from humiliation or harassment from a woman in the workplace, even if you bring a complaint against her that may or may not entertained by the Company based on your personal WhatsApp chat that has no relation with your work or workplace. However, you can take legal action against her for using derogatory words that malign or damage your reputation and social image if you can prove it before the Court. Any person who feels his reputation has been damaged by defamatory statements can sue for defamation under Section 356 of BNS that replaced Section 499 of IPC. The grounds for a defamation case include 1) A defamatory statement that has been made against a person, either written (libel) or spoken (slander), and 2) The statement was published or communicated to a third party. 3) The statement caused harm to his/her reputation, 4) There is no valid defense or justification for the defamatory statement. Defamation is a civil wrong where the individual rights of a person are infringed. A person can either file a civil suit against the person for defamation or can initiate criminal proceedings by filing a complaint as the remedy to defamation under Section 356 of BNS. If a person is found guilty of criminal defamation, he can be sentenced to imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both under Section 500 of IPC replaced by Section 356(2) of BNS. If required, hire an Advocate to navigate the issues in the right way. But it is advisable to try to resolve the issue amicably with mutual understanding, otherwise, personal disputes between colleagues may adversely affect the work culture and working environment of the workplace letting you both face legal/administrative actions from the Company following its service rules or policies.

question: My mother gets a family pension (my father passed away while in service) of more than 8 lakhs am I still eligible for OBC Non Creamy Layer Certificate?( Warangal, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,The eligibility for an OBC NCL certificate is determined based on the annual income of the applicant's parents if the income falls below Rs.8 lakh in a financial year. Regardless of sectors of employment either Public or Private, if the parent's income exceeds the threshold income limit, his son/daughter is not considered eligible for an OBC NCL Certificate. The wards of central Govt. Employees and the employees themselves are eligible for the OBC NCL certificate if they qualify the following criteria:- 1) Parents' income doesn't exceed Rs. 8 lakh per annum altogether. For the purpose of income, income from Salary and Agriculture should not be considered. 2) Group C and Group D employees even if their income exceeds 8 lakhs can apply for OBC NCL reservation because the salary and agriculture income is not counted as income. 3) If an employee becomes a Group A officer after his 40 years of age and income ( salary is not counted as income) below 8 lacks can also apply. 4) If the employee itself likes to apply for the higher post under OBC, Note only income of parents is counted for OBC status and not the applicants. As per the DOPT circular no. 36033/5/2004-EStt(Res) dated 14/10/2004, page 5, Clause 7, applicable to a government employee, it is clarified that if the father of sons or daughters is directly recruited in Class - III/Group C or Class - IV/Group D employees and he gets into Class - 1/Group -A at the age of 40 or earlier his sons or daughters shall not be treated to be falling in creamy layer category regardless of the income that exceeds the threshold limit of Rs.8 lakh p.a. The wards of Group C and Group D government employees, even if their income exceeds the threshold limit, can apply for OBC NCL Certificates because income from Salary and Agriculture is not counted as their income. So, if you meet the qualifying criteria, you can apply for an OBC NCL Certificate to the concerned authority.

question: I was terminated when i was 30week pregnant and i submitted all company asset on sep 25. I have been trying to get releiving letter and have not received yet. The duration of maternity leave for both first and second-time mothers is 6 months or 26 weeks. This leave can be availed either before or within 6 months from the expected date of delivery of the child. Further, be informed that termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Any Termination of a workman is covered under the Industrial Disputes Act and it falls under âRetrenchmentâ. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute directly before the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication provided he/she is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. Otherwise, in case he/she is holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, he/she has to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter. 2) As far as my google obtained knowledge goes, the contract is enforceable because the employer wants to recover the cost of training an employee, so if i am leaving my job as a under training employee, will i have to pay the penalty?
3) I have no copies of the contract I signed. Is that even legal?

I really just need some advise as to what I can do. Please help.

(p.s. i work in mumbai, and 25k salary here is literally jst fulfiling my expenses and i work 11-8, travel 1 hour to work and have weekends working.)( Mumbai, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear client,It sounds like you're in a difficult situation.  Employment bonds can be tricky, and the lack of clarity in your contract makes it even more complicated.If your employment contract does not specify the duration of the training period, your employer cannot arbitrarily extend it without justification. Since there are no clear training parameters in the contract, it seems like they are misusing the term "training" to delay your full salary.If you are performing all the duties of a regular employee, you should not be classified as a trainee indefinitely.You can ask HR in writing for clarity on when your training officially ends and what criteria determine the transition to full employment.A court would likely interpret the lack of a defined training period against the employer. It would be hard for them to justify an extended "training" period while you're doing full-fledged work.As you've researched, employment bonds are often enforceable to recover reasonable training costs. However, the key word is "reasonable.""Under Training" Argument: If you're genuinely still in training (and it's been a reasonable time), the employer might have a stronger case for recovering some costs. However, given your situation (performing full duties, no clear training structure), this argument is weak.The fact that you're still receiving the training salary, even after 5 months, further weakens their case. It suggests they haven't incurred significant costs beyond your salary, which is already low. The Rs. 75,000 penalty seems excessive given your salary and the unclear training situation.You have grounds to challenge the penalty. You can argue that the training period was undefined, you were performing regular duties, and the penalty is disproportionate to any actual training costs.It is absolutely your right to have a copy of the contract you signed. An employer cannot legally withhold this from you. Demand a copy immediately. This is crucial for understanding your obligations and rights. If they refuse, this is a very bad sign for them legally.What You Can Do:Demand Contract Copy (First and Foremost): This is your priority. Put your request in writing (email or letter) and keep a record of it.Consult with a Lawyer: This is highly recommended. An employment lawyer in Mumbai can review your situation, advise you on your legal rights, and help you negotiate with your employer. They can also help you if the employer tries to take legal action.Document Everything: Keep records of everything: emails, pay slips, work schedules, any verbal instructions, and notes about your responsibilities.With legal counsel, you can negotiate a mutual release from the bond. You can offer to repay a reasonable amount (far less than Rs. 75,000) if you feel it's necessary to avoid a legal battle. Given your circumstances, you might even be able to leave without paying anything.

question: my father salary income is 12 lakhs(Private Sector Employee) Year 2024-25 but my mother lost 7 lakh in share market till date of current year 2024-25. Can I get OBC NCL Certificate if I apply after 1st April? Note : Last 2 Year Income of my parent is more than 8 lakh.( Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,The eligibility for an OBC NCL certificate is determined based on the annual income of the applicant's parents if the income falls below Rs.8 lakh in a financial year. Regardless of sectors of employment either Public or Private, if the parent's income exceeds the threshold income limit, his son/daughter is not considered eligible for an OBC NCL Certificate. The wards of central govt Employees and the employees themselves are eligible for the OBC NCL certificate if they qualify following:- 1) Parents' income doesn't exceed Rs. 8 lakh per annum altogether. For the purpose of income, income from Salary and Agriculture should not be considered. 2) Group C and Group D employees even if their income exceeds 8 lahks can apply for OBC NCL reservation because the salary and agriculture income are not counted as income. 3) If an employee becomes a Group A officer after his 40 years of age and income ( salary is not counted as income) below 8 lacks can also apply. 4) If the employee itself likes to apply for the higher post under OBC, Note only income of parents is counted for OBC status and not the applicants. Loss in the share market has no bearing/significance on the Income/Wealth test for the issue of the OBC Certificate. If required, you may refer to the DOPT circular no. 36033/5/2004-EStt(Res) dated 14/10/2004 available on the official website of the DOPT.

question: My brother has done dual employment in 2021 during covid as he has got two offers with same joining date. answer: Dear Client,There is no overarching law that prohibits a person from doing multiple jobs. But, before joining another Company you are required to tender your resignation from the earlier company and obtain a relieving letter that eventually caused the dual employment or overlapping of service. A joint declaration form(JDF) is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer jointly sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts by default. To resolve the issue of dual employment/overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly/discrepancy arising out of the date of appointment and date of exit of an employee in EPF records. For lack of cooperation from the employers who are duty-bound to correct the records of member employees in EPF records, an individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). or filing a complaint offline in the office of the Regional PF Commissioner concerned. question: My employer was an exempt Trust for PF while I was in service from 1985 till  April2021 . Kept PF with employer for 3 years. PF exemption was surrendered in May2022 by employer. Took one year for transfer of PF to EPFO. During Final settlement in April2024 lot of irregularities related to service records were observed. Corrected one by one . Settlement happened in three parts viz .May, July  & Sept24. Can I claim Interest on this amount for delayed period( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,The members after switching over from one covered establishment to another do not get the funds transferred to their present account. As a result, the old account becomes inoperative after 36 months. If the employee under EPFO has not withdrawn or transferred his funds after switching jobs for 36 months, no interest rate will be credited to the account of a member from the first day of it becoming inoperative i.e. from the 37th month. Earlier, the union government had stopped crediting interest rates in the inoperative accounts of EPF subscribers from 1 April 2011. The Central Govt. in the year 2014 has decided to credit interest on claims if the settlement takes more than 30 days and the funds lying inactive in the Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has approved a revision to the rules governing interest payments within the EPF scheme. The board unanimously resolved to modify the interest payment date to align it with the date of settlement. This decision was reached during the 236th meeting of the CBT on November 30, 2024. The decision made by the CBT stipulates that interest on EPF will be disbursed to members up to the settlement date.

question: My employer is denying to pay my salary as I am on notice period. But as per the terms and conditions of the job agreement during my appointment they have kept my educational certificates. answer: Dear Client,An employer cannot stop an employee's monthly salary while he has tendered his resignation and is serving a notice period in terms of an offer/appointment letter. Regardless of the reason, upon cessation of employment, an employee is entitled to an experience certificate, relieving letter, and F & F settlement dues from the employer within 30 days of the last working days (LWD), and denial of these amounts to unfair labour practices. Even, an employer cannot withhold the original certificates of an outgoing employee which also amounts to unfair labour practices on the part of the Employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance and additionally, you can file an application under Section 33C(2) of the I D Act before the Labour Court concerned claiming your F & F Settlement dues receivable to you post-resignation from the employer/Company along with interest. Further, SAMADHAN Portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to facilitate the filing of industrial disputes by the workmen, employers and trade unions under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The online portal has a user-friendly interface and has enhanced transparency and efficiency of grievance resolution for all stakeholders. The workmen/trade unions/management can file their disputes and claims by logging into the portal through the UMANG app and also by visiting the nearest Common Services Centres. Be informed that to restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. If required, hire an Advocate experienced in service matters to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: Received assurance on onboarding but then the company turned out. There is a company based out of Chennai who hired me through campus placement. Firstly they gave me LOI with expiry of 31st July which was extended to September then to December. They also sent me multiple mails saying I would be onboarded in the month of August/September. But after my LOI expired in December they stopped responding to my mails and calls. They even did not give clarity whether my offer is revoked or not. They have just completely ignored us and this is costing me my future.( Chennai, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,A Letter of Intent (LOI) is a document used in the hiring process to outline the terms and conditions of a job offer. It is usually written by an employer to a candidate and includes information about the job title, salary, benefits, job responsibilities, start date, and work schedule. A letter of intent (LOI) issued by an employer to a potential candidate indicates only the employer's intention to issue an offer of employment later. A Division Bench of the Honâble Supreme Court in the matter of South Eastern Coalfields Ltd. & Ors. vs. S. Kumarâs Associates AKM (JV) held that an LOI indicated merely a partyâs intention to enter into a contract, and no binding relationship was concluded thereby unless an unambiguous agreement was clear from the terms of the LOI. Recently, while addressing concerns about onboarding, Capgemini clarified that the candidates selected on-campus had been issued only LOIs, which per se, were not offers of employment, and Capgeminiâs onboarding would be based on its staffing requirements. While a LOI outlines the preliminary understanding between two parties before a formal agreement is finalized and is non-binding, an offer letter is considered a binding agreement once the candidate accepts it, forming a contract of employment. So, when the Company is not responding to your calls or queries about your status of employment, it means that they are not interested in extending the tenure of LOI and that eventually bars the issue of an offer later. Thus, in the absence of a valid contract between the parties, no legal remedy is feasible as of now.

Dear Client,As per the Ministry of Finance Office Memo No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June 1965, the resignation is treated as a technical resignation where a Government servant has applied through proper channels for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met, even if the Government servant has not mentioned the word âTechnicalâ while submitting his resignation. The benefit of past service, if otherwise admissible under rules, may be given in such cases. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation and the benefit of past service will not be admissible. The benefit of past service is allowed in such cases subject to the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government servant should intimate the details of such application immediately on their joining; (ii) the Government servant at the time of resignation should specifically make a request, indicating that he is resigning to take up another appointment under the Government for which he applied before joining the Government service; (iii) the authority accepting the resignation should satisfy itself that had the employee been in service on the date of application for the post mentioned by the employee, his application would have been forwarded through proper channel. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within 2 years or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. Being the position as stated above you may seek further clarification on the subject from the concerned Deptt (DOPT) or apply to the State Administrative Tribunal (SAT) constituted under the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1985. But before approaching SAT, you have to represent your grievance before the HOD concerned and if your grievance is not resolved or you are aggrieved with the reply of the HOD to your grievance, you can apply before the concerned Bench of the State Administrative Tribunal(SAT) following the procedure as prescribed under the State Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules. If required, you may hire an advocate to handle SAT matters and navigate the issue in the right way.

now they are claiming to take legal actions against me and threatening me that i will have to pay heavy compensation and they will make me work for the 6 months probation period as well as 3 months to notice period after that and their behavior has now become even more toxic and abusive , please help me as im the sole earning member in my family and have no saving to pay any heavy amount or fight any legal case( Thane, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 prohibits any agreement/contract in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement/contract will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, Further, SAMADHAN Portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment for facilitating filing of industrial disputes by the workmen, employers and trade unions under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The online portal has a user-friendly interface and has enhanced transparency and efficiency of grievance resolution for all stakeholders. The workmen/trade unions/management can file their disputes and claims by logging into the portal through the UMANG app and also by visiting the nearest Common Services Centres. But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter. If you are not financially sound enough to continue with litigation expenses, you can apply before the Member Secretary, State Legal Services Authority or Dist. Legal Services Authority seeking free legal services available to women under Sec.12(c) of the Legal Services Authority Act, 1987 to contest the cases in the Court for appropriate relief.

question:
Dear Sir,

I have recently resigned from my organisation after serving for 4yrs 8 months and 2 days. As I have checked on internet 4.8 yrs is eligible for grautity.  I have conveyed same to my HR but he is saying grautity is eligible only for 5 yrs or more.

Would just require an confirmation from an legal advisor for exact rule of Grautity as this is pending from 4 months from my old employer end.( Mumbai suburban, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,According to Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act of 1972, gratuity must be paid to an employee upon cessation of employment if he or she has rendered continuous service for five years or more. According to section 2A of the Act, an employee is said to be in continuous service for a period if he has for that period been in uninterrupted service including service which may be interrupted on account of accident, sickness, leave, absence from duty without leave, layoff, strike or a lock-out or cessation of work not due to any fault of employee. Section 4(2) of the Act provides that for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of 6 months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the prescribed rates. So, when you worked for a period of 4 years 8 months & 2 days in the Company, you are eligible for payment of gratuity by the employer. Under Rule 7(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Rules, 1972, an employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Act, or any person authorized, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, within thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form 'I' to the employer who is duty bound to disburse the gratuity within 30 days of cessation of employment of employee or claim made by an employee. After the completion of 30 days, the employer has to pay you not only the gratuity amount but also the simple interest accrued for the delay in payment of the gratuity. In case of denial of gratuity by the employer, serving a legal notice to the company, reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner and the Controlling Authority under the Act to file a complaint against the employer over non-payment of gratuity despite your eligibility to redress the grievance. Under Sub-Sec.5 of Section 7 of the Act, the Controlling Authority is empowered with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to try the claim of the applicant and pass an order/direction on the claim petition. If required, you may hire the service of an Advocate experienced in service matters to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: I have worked in an Organization for 4 years 6 months & 7 days, they have refused to pay Gratuity stating that I have worked for 4 years and 208 days instead of 4 years and 240 days... is it correct? in spite of the fact that Gratuity been included in my CTC?( Chennai, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,According to Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act of 1972, gratuity must be paid to an employee upon cessation of employment if he or she has rendered continuous service for five years or more. According to section 2A of the Act, an employee is said to be in continuous service for a period if he has for that period been in uninterrupted service including service which may be interrupted on account of accident, sickness, leave, absence from duty without leave, layoff, strike or a lock-out or cessation of work not due to any fault of employee. Section 4(2) of the Act provides that for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of 6 months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the prescribed rates. So, when you worked for a period of 4 years 6 months & 7 days in the Company, you are eligible for payment of gratuity by the employer. Under Rule 7(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Rules, 1972, an employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Act, or any person authorized, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, within thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form 'I' to the employer who is duty bound to disburse the gratuity within 30 days of cessation of employment of employee or claim made by an employee. After the completion of 30 days, the employer has to pay you not only the gratuity amount but also the simple interest accrued for the delay in payment of the gratuity. In case of denial of gratuity by the employer, serving a legal notice to the company, reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner and the Controlling Authority under the Act to file a complaint against the employer over non-payment of gratuity despite your eligibility to redress the grievance. Under Sub-Sec.5 of Section 7 of the Act, the Controlling Authority is empowered with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to try the claim of the applicant and pass an order/direction on the claim petition. If required, you may hire the service of an Advocate experienced in service matters to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: I had worked for an MNC and left after 3.5 months due to medical issue because my TL was not supporting me and when i asked him to provide wfh for few days he refused, so i resigned from the organization on 10 nov 2022 with proper notice and medical documents and left the job and found another WFH opportunity and joined the organization on 14th Nov, also my TL talk to the HR of new company for BGV but still he didn't inform the HR that i am not reporting to the office after 2 years when i went for another company interview i came to knew that my last working day of that particular company is updated after 2 months that on 8 jan due to which its showing dual employment in my organization. Now when i contact the company they are asking me to pay the recovery amount of rs111000, which is a big amount to pay back to the company. Please suggest what i can do best in this case.( Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,Before joining another Company you are required to tender your resignation and to obtain a relieving letter from the earlier company serving the notice period as per the terms of employment that eventually caused the overlapping of service. The overlapping in service concerning previous and present establishments and any anomaly or discrepancy in EPF records of any registered member may be grounds for future disputes. When your EPF record shows an anomaly in the joining and exit date in both the previous and present Company which is contradictory, then until and unless those anomalies are rectified by the concerned employers, PF records will show overlapping or dual employment. A joint declaration form is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. An employee cannot update the service history. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database, he should contact their present or previous employers and get it corrected. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of dual employment/overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly/discrepancy arising out of date of appointment and date of exit of an employee in EPF records. For lack of cooperation from the employers who are duty-bound to correct the records of member employees in EPF records, an individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). or filing a complaint offline in the office of the Regional PF Commissioner concerned. If the complaint is not resolved even on receipt of JDF, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief yields from the office of the PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief.

question:
I am a permanent employee of a public sector bank. During my service I got some spine related medical issue and I am on leave for the last 3 years (out of this 2 years on medical leave and 1 year unauthorized absence) and I have still not joined my organisation. During this period I have also suffered from mental health issue and for which I have received 15% permanent disability for mental health.
My organization follows the guidelines of RPWD act 2016 (act for disabled) wherein it is mentioned that âNo Government establishment shall dispense with or reduce in rank, an employee who acquires a disability during his or her service. Provided that, if an employee after acquiring disability is not suitable for the post he was holding, shall be shifted to some other post with the same pay scale and service benefits: Provided further that if it is not possible to adjust the employee against any post, he may be kept on a supernumerary post until a suitable post is available or he attains the age of superannuation, whichever is earlierâ.
I seek clarification for the following:
Q1.- The wordings of the above clause âDuring the serviceâ means the employee should be on duty while he acquired disability or is it applicable for someone who is in service but not on duty ie someone who is on leave. 
Q2- The law applies to all persons with disability or only for people with Benchmark disability, as in my case the disability is less than 40%.
Q3 Whether the bank can terminate me in this case.
Please guide me as it is very important for my service.( Mumbai suburban, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act was enacted in the year 2016 and came into force on 19th April 2017. Individuals having 40% or more disability can apply for a disability certificate, provided their disability falls under the categories specified under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. So, when your disability falls below the threshold limit, you are not eligible to claim benefits available under the said Act. A supernumerary post is a post created for accommodating a permanent officer. till he is absorbed substantively in a regular permanent post, it should not be created. for an indefinite period as other permanent posts are, but should be created for a definite and fixed period sufficient for the purpose in view. Tenure in the Supernumerary post will not ordinarily exceed 2 years. As per O M No. 1301 513/2002-Estt.(I,), Government of India, Ministry of Personnel, P.G.& Pensions, Department of Personnel & Trainingdated i10th January 2004, the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment (Disabilities Div.) has amended Section 47 of the Persons with Disabilities Act 1995 and under the amended provisions: 1) No establishment shall dispense with or reduce ill rank an employee who acquires a disability during his service and the employee who has acquired disability if is not suitable for the post he was holding, could be shifted to some other post wit11 the same pay scale & service benefits. In case it is not possible to adjust him against any post, he may be kept on a supernumerary post until a suitable post is available or he attains the age of superannuation, whichever is earlier. 2) No promotion shall be denied to a person merely on the grounds of his disability. Provided that the appropriate govt. may having regard to the type of work carried out in any establishment, by Notification and subject to such conditions, if any as may be specified in such Notification, exempt any establishment from the provision of this section. This notification of DOPT is almost relevant in your case which you may access on the website of DOPT and take steps accordingly. Hope it helps.

I hope you're doing well. I am writing to seek clarification regarding the recent actions taken by the company in placing me on a 60-day notice period. I would appreciate it if you could help me understand the following points:

Reason for Notice Period: I was informed that the reason for placing me on a 60-day notice period is because I have not reported to the office, as I have been working from home. However, when I asked for formal communication or instructions regarding this requirement, I did not receive any clear response. I was never formally asked or informed to report to the office. I would like to understand why this reason is being cited when no such communication was shared with me.

Redeployment and Resignation: In the email from HR, it was mentioned that I am being placed in the redeployment pool, along with the statement that I am on a 60-day notice period. I was not given a direct explanation of this process or what it entails. Additionally, I did not formally resign, and I have not agreed to leave the company. I would like to know why my resignation is being assumed without my acceptance.

Can They Lay Me Off Without a Valid Reason?: Given the points above, I would like to know if it is legal for the company to lay me off without providing a valid reason or proper explanation. The reason mentioned, regarding my reporting to the office, seems to be invalid based on the lack of prior communication.

Notice Period Without Acceptance: Can the company force a notice period without my acceptance? Even if I do not accept the terms, will the company proceed with my layoff once my 60-day notice period concludes?

I would greatly appreciate your prompt response and clarification on these matters, as I am seeking to understand my position and options moving forward.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your reply.( South Delhi, Delhi )
answer: Dear Client,A termination may be considered illegal and unjustified if it breaches the terms of the contract or appointment letter by either party to the said contract. Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Any Termination of a workman is covered under the Industrial Disputes Act and it falls under âRetrenchmentâ. In the case of Punjab Land Development Corporation Vs Labour Court, 1990 (II) LLJ, 70 SC, the Supreme Court held that The expression âretrenchmentâ is not to be understood in its narrow, natural and contextual meaning, but is to be understood in its wider, literal meaning to mean termination of service of a workman for any reason whatsoever. Further, in the case of Santosh Gupta Vs State Bank of Patiala AIR 1980 SC 1219, the Supreme Court ruled that the expression retrenchment must include every termination of the services of a workman by an act of the employer. Even as per Clause 13(1) of the model Standing Order under Industrial Employment(Standing Orders) Act, 1946, for terminating the employment of a permanent workman, notice in writing shall be given either by the employer or the workman one month's notice in the case of monthly rated workmen and two weeks' notice in the case of other workmen; one month's or two week's pay, as the case may be, may be paid in lieu of notice. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman serving a legal notice to the employer can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. Otherwise, in case he is holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, he has to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter. If you are an employee of the IT Company then be informed that to restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947.

question: I have resigned on may-24. Company has pay to me variable pay for the FY 23-24. But they have not settled my veriable pay and now they are denying to pay veriable pay. I was eligible and it is included in my CTC. What will be the option I have( Mumbai suburban, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Variable pay or compensation is determined based on two main factors â the employee's performance and the company's overall performance. An employee becomes eligible to get variable pay in terms of employment only if he is on the payroll as on LWD(last working day) for the month the quarterly variable is paid. There are four quarters in a financial year. If the employee's LWD is on or after 30th June(for the quarter of April to June), he will receive it, else not. It appears from the query that quit the job on the 24th of May. So, when you tendered your resignation on 24th May, you were eligible for variable pay from the Company for the preceding financial year(2023-24) and the fraction quarter prior to resignation and the question does not arise at all to withhold the variable pay which is a part of CTC because you are already released on cessation of your relationship with the Company post-resignation. In the given situation, you just serve a legal notice to your Company demanding for disbursement of F & F dues including variable pay for the eligible period. In case the matter is not resolved, then visit the office of the Labour Commissioner or the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishment concerned to file a complaint against the Company for adopting unfair labor practices for redressal of your grievance provided you are a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the I D Act and simultaneously file an application under Sec:33C(2) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 before the State Govt. Labour Court for recovery of entire dues receivable from the Company on resignation. Otherwise, if you are holding a position of manager or administrative officer in the company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court for appropriate relief in the matter. Reach out to an Advocate handling service matters for guidance and steps to resolve the issue in the right way.

question:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I have recently been offered a position in another Central University on a lien vacancy, which is likely to be confirmed. My current organization, however, is not willing to retain my lien and has decided to relieve me on a technical resignation basis, despite the fact that I applied through the proper channel.

The leave and lien rules followed by my organization are similar to those outlined by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), which state that retaining a lien is a right of the employee. Based on these rules, denying a lien request seems incorrect.

As the last date to join the new organization is approaching, I am considering joining the new post and simultaneously filing a petition in court to retain my lien. This would ensure that I can revert to my permanent position if the new post on lien is not confirmed.

I seek your guidance on the following:

    Is it advisable to join the new organization under these circumstances while pursuing legal action to retain my lien?
    Based on the DoPT rules and precedents, what are the chances of success in court for retaining my lien?

Thank you for your time and assistance. I look forward to your advice.( Sundargarh, Orissa )
answer: Dear Client,As per Office Memo No.DOPT-1669266628362 dated 24 November 2022, issued by the Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India, and the Ministry of Finance OM No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June, 1965, read with proviso to FR 22-B, in cases of appointment of a Government servant to another post in Government on acceptance of technical resignation in the existing post, it may be informed that the resignation is treated as a technical formality where a Government servant has applied through a proper channel with a NOC for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign from the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. answer: Dear Client,From the prolonged contents of the query, it is unclear what type of legal remedies for a cause of action you sought from a counsel. However, be informed that a complaint can be filed with Lokpal of India in terms of provisions under 2(e) of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, for the offenses alleged to have been committed by a public servant under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 such as offences relating to public servant being bribed, taking undue advantage to influence public servant by corrupt or illegal means or by the exercise of personal influence, Offence relating to bribing of a public servant, Public servant obtaining (undue advantage), without consideration from person concerned in proceeding or business transacted by such public servant, Criminal misconduct by a public servant. In terms of provisions under Section 53, of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, a complaint should be made within seven years from the date on which the offense mentioned in the complaint is alleged to have been committed. A complaint is required to be filed in the prescribed form annexed with the Lokpal (Complaint) Rules, 2020. The complaint can be filed online through the Lokpal Online portal. A fillable complaint form is also available at (https://lokpal.gov.in/pdfs/complaint_form.docx). Under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, sanction for prosecution is required for an offence punishable under Sections 7, 10, 11, 13, 15 of the Act, while under Section 197(1) Cr. P.C. sanction is required for an offence committed by a public servant while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty, and not otherwise. After the amendment of the Prevention of Corruption Act, in 2018, it significantly extended the provisions of PCA and gave it the required edge to tackle bribery/corruption involving commercial entities/private companies. According to Section 9 of the amended Act, a commercial organization can be held liable âif any person associated with such commercial organization gives or promises to give any undue advantage to a public servantâ with an intent to obtain or retain business or any advantage for that commercial organization. This provision covers all types of entities (including domestic companies, foreign companies, and partnerships) doing business in India. Thus, while the PCA, 1988 applied to public sector employees, the Act has been amended to encompass situations where private organizations and individuals can also be held accountable for indulging in corrupt practices. Further, the CBI investigates cases of corruption in compliance with the provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, under the supervision of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). This can include cases of bribery, extortion, and other forms of corruption. The CBI has a special division called the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB). This branch handles the investigation of corruption-related cases. The CBI can initiate suo moto investigations on the basis of information received from the public, the media, or other sources. CBI lays great emphasis on catching corrupt public servants who demand and take bribes. The process of catching such corrupt public servants red-handed while they demand and take bribes is popularly called the 'trap'. It is not a legal term. A set procedure has been devised in CBI to lay a trap against a corrupt public servant. The evidence collected during the process of trap is placed before the court along with the charge sheet and is quite important in securing the conviction of the public servant charged with corruption. So, given the proposition of relevant laws, you may choose the recourse/steps that suit your grievance most in the prevailing situation, If required, hire an experienced Advocate to navigate the issues in the right way.

Is this a valid consequence. If not, how can we address this?( Mahbubnagar, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,As per Office Memo No.DOPT-1669266628362 dated 24 November 2022, issued by the Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India, and the Ministry of Finance OM No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June, 1965, read with proviso to FR 22-B, in cases of appointment of a Government servant to another post in Government on acceptance of technical resignation in the existing post acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. The benefit of past service is allowed in such cases subject to the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government servant should intimate the details of such application immediately on their joining; (ii) the Government servant at the time of resignation should specifically make a request, indicating that he is resigning to take up another appointment under the Government for which he applied before joining the Government service; (iii) the authority accepting the resignation should satisfy itself that had the employee been in service on the date of application for the post mentioned by the employee, his application would have been forwarded through proper channel. In your father's case if these qualifying criteria are met and despite his entitlement, if the reduction of wages is caused, then your father can make a grievance before the HOD and if that grievance yields no result, your father can approach the concerned bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) by filing an application in Form - I under sub-rule 1 Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 seeking appropriate relief in the matter. question: Sir, I am a army person and will retire after 2 years and I have 3 child, so can i will  be eligible for central govt job after retirement.( Jaipur, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,The Ex-Seerviceman (Re-employment in Central Civil Services and Posts) Rules, 1979 as modified by the Gazette Notification dated 2P Oct. 1986., defines an ex-serviceman as a person who has served in any rank whether as combatant or non-combatant in the Regular Army, Navy and Air force of the Indian Union. Ten percent of the vacancies in the posts of the level of Assistant Commandant in all para-military forces, ten percent of the vacancies in each of the categories of Group 'C' and of such posts in each Group 'C' service; and twenty percent of the vacancies in each of the categories of Group 'D' posts and of such posts in each Group 'D' service, including permanent vacancies filled initially temporarily and temporary vacancies which are likely to be made permanent or are likely to continue for three months and more, to be filled by direct recruitment in any year shall be reserved for being filled by ex-servicemen. There is no specific mention of 3 children of an ex-serviceman barring him from availing the reservation of central Govt jobs post-retirement. However, in a recent judgment, the Supreme Court upheld the decision of the Rajasthan Government to disqualify a candidate from applying to a police constable post for having more than two children. The Court held that Rule 24(4) of the Rajasthan Police Subordinate Service Rules, 1989, which provides that âno candidate shall be eligible for appointment to the service who has more than two children on or after 01.06.2002. Rule Disqualifying Candidate Having More Than 2 Children From Govt Job Doesn't Violate Constitution of India. So, considering the rulings of the Supreme Court, you should clarify the matter from the Department of Personnel and Training(DOPT), MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS, Government of India.

question: I have did dual employment without knowing it will effect my career my PF is getting overlap now and no one is hiring. Have approached regional commissioner seeking help but no one is helping to resolve this issue please help( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,Before joining another Company you are required to tender your resignation and to obtain a relieving letter from the earlier company serving the notice period as per the terms of employment that eventually caused the overlapping of service. The overlapping in service in respect of previous and present establishment and any anomaly or discrepancy in EPF records of any registered member may be a ground for future dispute. When your EPF record shows an anomaly in the joining and exit date in both the previous and present Company which is contradictory, then until and unless those anomalies are rectified by the concerned employers, PF records will show overlapping or dual employment. A joint declaration form is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. An employee cannot update the service history. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database, he should contact their present or previous employers and get it corrected. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly arising out of the date of appointment and date of discharge in EPF records. An individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). Once you succeed in wiping out the stigma of dual employment from your EPF records with the cooperation of your previous and present employer, your scope of employment with other companies will be restored with clean employment records. If the complaint is not resolved even on receipt of JDF, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief yields from the office of the PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief. In case of non-cooperation from both previous and current employers which amounted to unfair labour practice, you may bring the matter to the notice of the the concerned Labour Commissioner or Asst. Labour Commissioner/LEO/Chief Inspector(Shops and Establishment) for a resolution in the matter.
