question: I decided to quit TCS after 5 days, but I don't want to pay the bond amount, but the HR told me that he will only accept the resignation mail if I mention paying the bond amount. What should i do?( Noida, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,Please go through the terms and conditions of your appointment letter and the service bond executed by you that governs your relationship with the company. A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of service bonds can be challenged by invoking Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (service/employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the service/employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking desired relief in the matter. If required, reach out to an Advocate experienced in service matters for guidance and steps. Be informed that to restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. Further, the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the case of Godrej and Boyce Manufacturing Company Ltd. v. Shivkranti Kamgar Sanghatana, 2024 SCC OnLine Bom 938, decided on 28-03-2024 ruled out that the nature of duties and functions is the determining factor in ascertaining âworkmanâ under S. 2(s) of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

question: I have been terminated from a public listed company within 1 month of joining and that too without any prior notice or any reason of termination. How I can compensation till my retirement from the company, as I joined company at the age of 56 and retirement age is 60 year. I was appointed in a senior management  position.( Jaipur, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,A termination may be considered illegal and unjustified if it breaches the terms of the contract or appointment letter by either party to the said contract. You joined a company(PSU) at the age of 56 years and were terminated after a month without serving any show-cause notice or holding any inquiry into misconduct, if any. Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Any Termination of a workman is covered under the Industrial Disputes Act and it falls under âRetrenchmentâ. In the case of Punjab Land Development Corporation Vs Labour Court, 1990 (II) LLJ, 70 SC, the Supreme Court held that The expression âretrenchmentâ is not to be understood in its narrow, natural and contextual meaning, but is to be understood in its wider, literal meaning to mean termination of service of a workman for any reason whatsoever. Further, in the case of Santosh Gupta Vs State Bank of Patiala AIR 1980 SC 1219, the Supreme Court ruled that the expression retrenchment must include every termination of the services of a workman by an act of the employer. In that scenario, serving a legal notice to the Employer/company, the terminated employee being a PSU employee, can approach the concerned bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) by filing an application in Form - I under sub-rule 1 of Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 seeking appropriate order in the matter and if the CAT passes any adverse order, you can challenge the order through an appeal before the High Court seeking appropriate relief based on the merit of the dispute. Reach out to an Advocate experienced in CAT matters for necessary advice and steps.

question:
My father worked as a permanent employee in the Indian Railways. He joined in 2002 and retired in 2012. Before becoming a permanent employee, he worked in a contractor role. As per a Supreme Court ruling regarding contractor-to-permanent employee transitions, he officially should have been recognized as joining in 2000. However, due to financial issues and some discrepancies raised by the officeâsuch as an incorrect nameâthey delayed his regularization.

Now that my father has passed away, my mother is the dependent. I am considering filing a case under your supervision to address this matter. A similar issue occurred with one of my father's colleagues, who filed a case and is now receiving their rightful pension and arrears.

I would appreciate your opinion on this matter and any advice you could provide regarding the next steps.

Looking forward to your response.( Asansol, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,The Hon'ble Supreme Court has ruled that casual workers are also entitled to social security benefits as there should be no discrimination between contractual and permanent employees by their employer. The services of Contractual Employee can be counted towards qualifying service for Grant of Pension, Post Regularization as per Himachal Pradesh High Courtâs recent decision in Sheela Devi versus. State of HP & Ors. In CWPOA  No. 195/2019 by J Tarlok Singh Chauhan & J Chander Bhushan Barowalia.  As per Notification No. 26 (3)-Pension Unit/82, dated the 26th August, 1983 issued by Deptt. of Personnel & A.R, Govt. of India and published in the Gazette of India, dated the 10th September, 1983, as S.O. No. 3478, and as per Rue 5(3) of the Payment of Arrears of Pension (Nomination) Rules, 1983. every employee who is due to retire after the date of commencement of these rules shall submit the nomination, in triplicate, in Form "A" to the Head of Office or the Department from where he is retiring within three months before or after the date of retirement. According to sub-rule 7 of Rule 5, Nomination, fresh nomination or notice of modification of nomination shall take effect from the date of receipt thereof by the Pension Disbursing Authority or the Head of Office, as the case may be. Further, as per Rule 6, a nomination made under Rule 5 and accepted by the Pension Disbursing Authority or the Head of Office, shall be conclusive proof with regard to the person nominated to receive arrears of pension of the pensioner under these rules and the Office Memos are applicable to a pensioner under the new pension scheme subject to submission of Form I under Rule 10 within 6 months of resuming the govt. service or after retirement from the service. So, given the relevant notification and rules, first, be ensured whether your father complied with the provision of nomination in favour of your mother before or after his retirement from the service of railways or after the conversion of status of employment from contractual to permanent. In case such statutory formalities are complied with, you may escalate your grievance before the Secretary to the Ministry of Home Affairs (Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms) and the Ministry of Personnel Pension & Public Grievance Department of Pension & Pensionersâ Welfare either online or offline mode. In case no favorable or satisfactory response is received from the concerned Deptts, then you can consider filing an application before the Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) for redressal of the grievance following the provision of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 and the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987. Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 prescribes the procedure for applying before the Registrar of the concerned bench of the CAT.  So, try to get the matter reviewed by an expert professional before approaching the CAT.

question: I have worked in a manufacturing company for 9 years and as per Payslip my joining date is 1.05.2016 when my EPF account was started.I gave an immediate resignation email 4 months ago but they refused to give any acceptance and did not reply back to my mail . Can they refused to give gratuity as I resigned without service notice period and also I didn't have any contract or appointment letter mentioned to serve a notice period.( Kolkata, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,The question of serving a notice period does not arise in the absence of any specific stipulation in the appointment letter requiring an employee to serve a notice period upon submission of resignation. According to Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act of 1972, gratuity must be paid to an employee upon cessation of employment if he or she has rendered continuous service for five years or more. When you are in continuous service for more than 9 years before the resignation, you are eligible for payment of gratuity from the initial date of employment, i.e., 01/05/2016 to the date of your resignation. Section 4(2) of the Act provides that for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of 6 months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the prescribed rates. Under Rule 7(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Rules, 1972, an employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Act, or any person authorized, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, within thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form 'I' to the employer who is duty bound to disburse the gratuity within 30 days of cessation of employment of employee or claim made by an employee. After the completion of 30 days, the employer has to pay you not only the gratuity amount but also the simple interest accrued for the delay in payment of the gratuity. In case of denial of gratuity by the employer, serving a legal notice to the company, reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner and the Controlling Authority under the Act to file a complaint against the employer over non-payment of gratuity despite your eligibility to redress the grievance. Under Sub-Sec.5 of Section 7 of the Act, the Controlling Authority is empowered with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to try the claim of the applicant and pass an order/direction on the claim petition. If required, you may hire an Advocate experienced in service matters to navigate the issue in the right way.

question:
I am a central govt employee since 2 years. I have applied for state govt service and intimated the department for NOC. But they refused and I have mentioned in application form my current employer.
So in the document process they are asking me for NOC certificate 
So what I do now?( Dausa, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,As per Office Memo No.DOPT-1669266628362 dated 24 November 2022, issued by the Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India, and the Ministry of Finance OM No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June, 1965, read with proviso to FR 22-B, in cases of appointment of a Government servant to another post in Government on acceptance of technical resignation in the existing post. Be informed that the resignation is treated as a technical formality where a Government servant has applied through a proper channel with an NOC for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign from the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. Being the position as stated above you may seek further clarification on the subject from the concerned Deptt (DOPT). Hence it is advisable before moving ahead with litigation, you need to represent the grievance before the Head of the Deptt. for a resolution failing which, you can approach the concerned bench Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) seeking appropriate relief in the matter. Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 prescribes the procedure for applying before the Registrar of the concerned bench of the CAT. This forum has been established to adjudicate disputes concerning recruitment and conditions of service for persons appointed for public services. So, try to get the matter reviewed by an expert professional before challenging the action of the establishment before approaching the CAT.

However, be informed that recruitment, promotion, upgradation, etc. are the prerogatives of the concerned authority/establishment strictly followed based on an established recruitment policy and in exceptional cases following the Court's order. Any complaint or allegation over malpractice or unfair practice in the recruitment of manpower against an establishment shall not be entertained by a Court unless the alleged malpractice or unfairness in recruitment policy and practice appears on the face of the record. So, it is a very difficult and cumbersome exercise to prove such an allegation before the court. Only in case of deviation/discrimination/mala fide in the policy or rules, if appears on the face of the record, the High Court may entertain an appeal/petition challenging the recruitment policy/rules violating the well-established policy of the organization. Otherwise, a petition may be rejected at the stage of admission by the High Court.

I served 30 days of notice instead of 90 days and I told my manager before putting in the resignation. I submitted all assets assigned on my name.
Now he is sending me mails stating unauthorised absence- pretending like we never had those conversations.
What to do next in this case to get my FnF and exp letter along with gratuity( North Delhi, Delhi )
answer: Dear Client,Withholding of relieving letter/experience certificate, F & F settlement dues of an outgoing employee amounted to victimization and unfair labour practice on the part of the Employer. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer are not valid and are to be void on contest. The employee has the right to resign from the employment for a better opportunity, even if there is a non-compete clause in the contract of employment or if he/she has agreed to serve the employer for a specific period under a service bond. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. Regardless of reasons, on cessation of employment, an employee is entitled to an experience certificate, relieving letter and F & F settlement dues including gratuity from the employer within 30 days of the last working days (LWD) and denial of which amounted to unfair labour practices. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter. If required, reach out to an experienced Advocate dealing with service matters to navigate the issue in the right way.

However, be informed that the whole object of granting a compassionate appointment is to enable the family to tide over the sudden crisis, relieve the deceased's family from financial poverty, and help it get over the emergency. Compassionate appointment is not a vested right or an alternate mode of employment. It is considered and granted strictly following the relevant rules and the scheme. Under the Compassionate Appointments Scheme, employment is offered to any one of the legal heirs of the deceased Public Servant of PSU (i.e.) Wife, Husband, Son, Daughter, Divorcee, Widowed daughter if qualified for the same in terms of rules of compassionate appointment. The eligibility for an appointment under the Scheme for Compassionate Appointment is updated on 02/08/2022 by the Deptt. of Personnel and Training(DOPT), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievance and Pension, Govt. of India wherein scope and eligibility for employment under the compassionate appointment scheme are explained in detail. The Supreme Courtâs judgment dated May 4, 1994 in the case of Umesh Kumar Nagpal vs. State of Haryana and others [JT 1994(3) S.C. 525] has ruled that offering compassionate appointment as a matter of course irrespective of the financial condition of the family of the deceased or medically retired Government servant is legally impermissible. Compassionate appointment cannot be granted after lapse of a reasonable period and it is not a vested right that can be exercised at any time in the future. The Supreme Court has also held in its judgment dated February 28, 1995 in the case of the Life Insurance Corporation of India vs. Mrs Asha Ramchandra Ambekar and others [JT 1994(2) S.C. 183] that the High Courts and Administrative Tribunals can not give direction for appointment of a person on compassionate grounds but can merely direct consideration of the claim for such an appointment. answer: Dear Sir,PF  PROVIDENT FUNDHow to solve the two UAN problem?Note that each person should have only one UAN number (like PAN), hence if you have multiple UAN, itâs not allowed and creates problem in the EPF system, because is no proper track. Hence, as soon as you come to know that there are multiple UAN assigned to you, you should cancel one of the UAN (mostly the old UAN) or should try to deactivate one of themProcess to deactivate old UANStep #1 â The first step if that you should start the EPF transfer for all the EPFâs which are not under the latest UAN generated. This can be done using the OTCP portal of EPFO . I am not going in details here, but first you need to make sure all the old EPFâs are transferred and linked to the new UAN.Step #2 â In the next step, the EPFO system will automatically identify those UAN for which the EPF transfers have happened and completed. Once they find the idle UAN, they will automatically deactivate that UAN. You donât have to do anything here. This deactivation process will take place from time to time as per decision taken by EPFO. Once the deactivation happens, your old member id (your old EPF accounts) will be linked to new UAN.If you are already sure that your past UAN does not have the EPF linked to them, then you can mail your old UAN number along with recent UAN to your employer and to[emailÂ protected]. They will verify your UANâs status and deactivate the old UAN.How To Merge Two Uan EPF AccountsWhat is UAN?Universal Account Number (UAN) is a unique 12-digit number that is given to each member of the Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). With the help of the UAN, PF members can easily manage their accounts. The Ministry of Employment and Labour under the guidance of the Government of India issues UAN to PF members. Irrespective of the organisation they work in, all Provided Fund (PF) information can be accessed in one place by PF members with the help of UAN.In earlier days, whenever an individual would join a new organization, he would be given a new PF account number. This made it difficult to keep a check on the updated PF balance. It was also difficult to track activities related to pay change and employees would find it challenging to check PF contribution against the updated pay. To tackle such issues, the UAN was introduced.UAN is a universal number that helps members to gather all the PF accounts linked to multiple IDs of various organizations in one place. By using UAN, the employee can withdraw and also transfer funds in the PF account.More Information on UANâ¢	The UAN is a unique number provided to all employees enrolled for PF benefit. This number is independent of employers and hence does not change even if an employee changes job.â¢	The employer can validate an employee by using his UAN in case KYC documents have been verified.â¢	Since the UAN facility is available online for all employees, no employer can deduct or hold off an employeeâs PF.â¢	An employee can validate the PF deposit made by the employer every month. He/she has to register as an EPF Member on the Portal by using the UAN provided.â¢	EPF passbook access is available through SMS. One can send EPFOHO UAN ENG to 7738299899 from the mobile number that has been registered with the EPFO.How to register the UAN?Here are a few easy steps to be followed for registering the UAN:â¢	Go to the EPF Member Portal.â¢	Click on âActivate UANââ¢	Enter all the information around UAN, such as member id, mobile number, Aadhaar, PAN, name, date of birth and e-mail idâ¢	Select âGet Authorization PINâ to fetch the PIN on the registered mobile numberâ¢	Provide this PIN for verifying the request.â¢	Set up a username and password on the UAN portal for future use.Common Reasons for Allotment of Two UANsIf an employee changes his job, a new EPF account is set up by the new organisation. All existing EPF accounts are auto-linked with the UAN of the employee. Hence, there are high chances that a new UAN is allotted to the employee at the time of moving between jobs. There could be multiple reasons for allotment of new UAN. Listed here are some of the common reasons:â¢	In case an employee has not disclosed his previous UAN â In case an employee changes his job, he must make sure to disclose his existing UAN and EPF account number (Member ID) to the new employer. In absence of disclosure of this information, the employer may open a fresh PF account along with a new UAN.â¢	Non-disclosure of âDate of Exitâ by the previous employer â During the process of EPF transfer to the new employer, the old employer must mention the date of exit in the ECR (Electronic Challan and Return). In case of the absence of this information promptly, the new organisation may allot a new UAN to the employee.Consequences of Holding Two UANsTwo active UANs is not permitted by law and is against the rules. A member must have only one UAN with all the EPF accounts linked to it. EPF accounts cannot be transferred among employees. However, an employee who has two UANs can request for his EPF account to be transferred from one UAN to another and ask his previous UAN to be closed. Thus, an EPF account linked with one UAN will have to be compulsorily transferred to another EPF account linked with a separate UAN.What Should an Employee Do?In recent years, there have been multiple cases of employees assigning different UANs (Universal Account Number) to employees. According to EPF rules, an individual should have only one UAN at any given point of time. The employeeâs EPF account must be linked to his UAN. In case he/she has been assigned two UANs, the previous one must be deactivated at the earliest.Two Methods to Merge Two UAN EPF AccountsEmployees who have been incorrectly allotted two UANs must get one of them deactivated (normally, the previous one). There are two ways of getting the UAN deactivated and the EPF account transferred to the correct and active UAN. Mentioned below are the two commonly used methods:Method 1â¢	Reach out to your employer or EPFO and report the issue at the earliestâ¢	You can write an email to[emailÂ protected]stating about your current and previous UANâ¢	EPFO will begin verification on the issue once it gets notified about the issueâ¢	Your previous UAN is then blocked and the existing UAN remains activeâ¢	After this, you have to submit a claim for transferring the EPF account (linked with the blocked UAN) to the new active account.This process can be time-consuming and the general resolution rate is said to be very low. Thus, EPFO has set up a new procedure which is expected to make things easier for a member. It will especially be helpful while merging two UANs and transferring EPF easily. Here is the new method which can be used by an employee with two UANs:Method 2â¢	After thorough identification, old UAN will be deactivated by EPFO once the transfer of the EPF to the new UAN is completeâ¢	Thus, the old UANs will be blocked automatically and an employeeâs previous member ID will be linked to the new or existing UANâ¢	SMS notification is sent for the deactivation to the employeeâs registered mobile numberâ¢	If the employee has been unable to activate his new UAN, he will be notified to activate it at the earliest to receive the status update of the accountâ¢	There could be instances where the employee gets PF arrears from the previous employer. In such situations, the arrear is credited to the new PF account which is linked with the new UAN.Advantages of UAN for EmployeesMinimum Employer Involvement in PF withdrawals:  With the presence of UAN, the employer involvement is significantly reduced since the PF accumulation from the old organization is auto-transferred to the new PF account after completion of KYC verification.No Need for Fund Transfer: An employee must furnish his UAN details and KYC to the new employer for transferring the old PF balance to the new PF account post verification.Manage via SMS Alerts: Employees will receive SMS as soon as a contribution is made by the employer towards PF. This is provided, the employee has registered on the UAN portal.How to use UAN for PF Transfer?The Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) constantly takes several measures to make the operation of EPF accounts easier for both the employer and employees. To keep up with the technological advancements, EPFO is constantly striving towards streamlining of processes about online EPF. This is especially applicable to PF transfer and withdrawal of PF which are considered to be tedious and time-consuming processes.EPFO introduced Universal Account Number (UAN), which is the blanket number for multiple Member Ids given to an individual by various employers. UAN allows the linking of multiple EPF Accounts (Member Id) provided to a single EPF member. It offers a range of services such as dynamically updated UAN card, updated PF passbook including all transfer-in details, facility to link previous membersâ ID with present ID, monthly SMS regarding credit of contribution in PF account and facility for auto-triggering transfer request on change of employment.Till recently, PF transfer could be done online by going to the âOnline Transfer Claim Portalâ. However, with the introduction of UAN, the transfer process has been revised and shifted under the âunified portalâ. For online PF transfer, here are some of the important points to note:â¢	An EPF member must have activated his UAN on the UAN portal and the registered mobile number used for activation should be in an active state.â¢	The Bank account number and IFSC code of the employee's bank account must be updated against the UAN. Updated Aadhar number and PAN is not mandatory for PF transfer requests.â¢	The employer must approve the e-KYC for transfer to be executed.â¢	The previous/current employer must have digitally registered authorized signatories on EPFO portal.â¢	PF account number related to previous and current employment of an employee should be updated in EPFO database.â¢	Single transfer requests per member ID can be accepted.FAQs1. What if I have two UAN numbers? Does it impact my EPF balance or transfer in any way?Two different UAN numbers for one employee is not accepted and is against the rules. If you happen to change jobs and move between organizations, you must request for transfer of PF account at the earliest.2. What is the expected timeline for merging two EPF accounts?It normally takes around 20 days from the date of the request to transfer one EPF account to the other.3. Is Form 13 a prerequisite for UAN transfer?Employees working in the corporate sector are required to submit Form 13 for EPF transfer to their new PF account at the time of job change.4. How is Form 13 used?Form 13 is primarily used for the transfer of Provident Fund from one account to another. Employees have to submit this form to their employers, upon which, the latter have to verify and approve the details furnished.

question: my employer give me suspension order without given any reason( Nanded, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,It is illegal and unfair on the part of an employer to suspend an employee without any reason or ground. An employer cannot suspend an employee without serving a show cause notice or chargesheet and without conducting an inquiry into the said show cause notice/chargesheet or without giving the delinquent employee to defend the allegation/misconduct. Such an action on the part of an employer amounts to victimization and unfair labour practice and violation of natural justice as well. As per Section 10A(1) in The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 where any workman is suspended by the employer pending investigation or inquiry into complaints or charges of misconduct against him, the employer shall pay to such workman subsistence allowance (a) at the rate of fifty percent of the wages which the workman was entitled to immediately preceding the date of such suspension, for the first ninety days of suspension; and (b) at the rate of seventy-five percent. of such wages for the remaining period of suspension if the delay in the completion of disciplinary proceedings against such workman is not directly attributable to the conduct of such workman. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the employer/company over alleged victimization and unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, Further, SAMADHAN Portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment for facilitating filing of industrial disputes online by the workmen, employers and trade unions under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The online portal has a user-friendly interface and has enhanced transparency and efficiency of grievance resolution for all stakeholders. The workmen/trade unions/stakeholders can file their disputes and claims by logging into the portal through the UMANG app and also by visiting the nearest Common Services Centres. The purpose of the Portal is also to minimize the confusion of workers under the applicability of labour laws, to eliminate the delay caused due to offline communication at various levels & to facilitate the workmen/unions/stakeholders in tracking their matters online and for centralized monitoring by the Ministry to bring transparency and efficiency. But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. question: I have not reporting from previous 05-May-2019  and joined next org on 13-May-2019 causing overlap issue in epfo portal. How can i solve this if the last 8 days in my first org is lop days in pf portal. Can pf office help me rectify this problem as the 1st org is not willing to give joint declaration and first org mentioned last working day in 21-May-2019 in pf portal.( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,There is no overarching law that prohibits a person from doing multiple jobs. But, before joining another Company you are required to tender your resignation from the earlier company and obtain a relieving letter that eventually caused the dual employment or overlapping of service. A joint declaration form(JDF) is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer jointly sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts by default. To resolve the issue of dual employment/overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly/discrepancy arising out of the date of appointment and date of exit of an employee in EPF records. For lack of cooperation from the employers who are duty-bound to correct the records of member employees in EPF records, an individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). or filing a complaint offline in the office of the Regional PF Commissioner concerned. If the complaint is not resolved even on receipt of JDF, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief yields from the office of the PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief.

question: I have been voluntary retired from SBI by their own ,in 2022.can  I get my job back( Jamshedpur, Jharkhand )

Commercial employment includes business and self-employment.

question:
I recently completed a (Performance Improvement Plan)PIP at my previous employer, Infosys, meeting all tasks and training requirements. Despite this, my evaluation was marked as failed without clear explanation. My manager didnât assign required accelerate tasks, though I applied for them, and I faced limited communication and feedback throughout the process.

After my evaluation, I requested documentation related to my PIP goals, criteria, and any communications about my performance. I also received a show cause notice without explanation, and my requests for clarification and documentation have gone unanswered.

Could you advise me on:

My legal right to access these documents.
Grounds to dispute an unfair PIP evaluation.
Next steps if the company continues to deny access to my documentation.( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,A performance improvement plan (PIP), also known as a performance action plan, is a tool to give an employee with performance deficiencies the opportunity to succeed. It is a good practice, followed by many employers to assess the potential abilities of an employee. In case the assigned task under PIP does not match your skill or efficiency, you should bring the matter to the notice of the Company. If you fail to cope with the PIP, the company may ask you to quit the job and if you quit in the course of PIP, you may lose getting any unemployment benefit or any severance package. In the given scenario, it may be suggested that you find other suitable jobs elsewhere that fit your skill and efficiency. Performance evaluation documents post-PIP are purely private and confidential and a candidate cannot access his own appraisal/assessments as a matter of right. It may be noted that recruitment, promotion, placement, transfer, upgradation etc. are the prerogatives and discretionary on the part of the management followed based on an established HR policy of the Company. Only in case of deviation/discrimination/mala fide in the HR rules/policy, if appears on the face of the record, the Courts or Tribunals may entertain an appeal challenging the well-established HR policy of the Company. Regardless of the sector or character of establishments either public or private, the recruitment of manpower is processed following its standing recruitment policy and recruitment of manpower is also a prerogative of the establishment. Any complaint or allegation over malpractice or unfair practice in the recruitment of manpower against an establishment shall not be entertained by a Court unless the alleged malpractice or unfairness in recruitment policy and practice appears on the face of the record. So, it is a very difficult and cumbersome exercise to prove such an allegation before the court.

question: In december 2022, i have joined as PA stenographer in district court and i have technically resigned to join state public service as PA stenographer in august 2024. As i have no lien can i revert back my parent department if they wish to take back me again.( Agartala, Tripura )
answer: Dear Client,As per the Ministry of Finance Office Memo No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June, 1965, the resignation is treated as a technical resignation where a Government servant has applied through proper channels for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met. The benefit of past service, if otherwise admissible under rules, may be given in such cases. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation and the benefit of past service will not be admissible. The benefit of past service is allowed in such cases subject to the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government servant should intimate the details of such application immediately on their joining; (ii) the Government servant at the time of resignation should specifically make a request, indicating that he is resigning to take up another appointment under the Government for which he applied before joining the Government service; (iii) the authority accepting the resignation should satisfy itself that had the employee been in service on the date of application for the post mentioned by the employee, his application would have been forwarded through proper channel. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. Being the position as stated above you may seek further clarification on the subject from the concerned Deptt (DOPT) or apply to the parent department for consideration.

answer: PF  PROVIDENT FUNDHow to solve the two UAN problem?Note that each person should have only one UAN number (like PAN), hence if you have multiple UAN, itâs not allowed and creates problem in the EPF system, because is no proper track. Hence, as soon as you come to know that there are multiple UAN assigned to you, you should cancel one of the UAN (mostly the old UAN) or should try to deactivate one of themProcess to deactivate old UANStep #1 â The first step if that you should start the EPF transfer for all the EPFâs which are not under the latest UAN generated. They will verify your UANâs status and deactivate the old UAN.How To Merge Two Uan EPF AccountsWhat is UAN?Universal Account Number (UAN) is a unique 12-digit number that is given to each member of the Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). With the help of the UAN, PF members can easily manage their accounts. The Ministry of Employment and Labour under the guidance of the Government of India issues UAN to PF members. Irrespective of the organisation they work in, all Provided Fund (PF) information can be accessed in one place by PF members with the help of UAN.In earlier days, whenever an individual would join a new organization, he would be given a new PF account number. This made it difficult to keep a check on the updated PF balance. It was also difficult to track activities related to pay change and employees would find it challenging to check PF contribution against the updated pay. To tackle such issues, the UAN was introduced.UAN is a universal number that helps members to gather all the PF accounts linked to multiple IDs of various organizations in one place. By using UAN, the employee can withdraw and also transfer funds in the PF account.More Information on UANâ¢	The UAN is a unique number provided to all employees enrolled for PF benefit. This number is independent of employers and hence does not change even if an employee changes job.â¢	The employer can validate an employee by using his UAN in case KYC documents have been verified.â¢	Since the UAN facility is available online for all employees, no employer can deduct or hold off an employeeâs PF.â¢	An employee can validate the PF deposit made by the employer every month. He/she has to register as an EPF Member on the Portal by using the UAN provided.â¢	EPF passbook access is available through SMS. One can send EPFOHO UAN ENG to 7738299899 from the mobile number that has been registered with the EPFO.How to register the UAN?Here are a few easy steps to be followed for registering the UAN:â¢	Go to the EPF Member Portal.â¢	Click on âActivate UANââ¢	Enter all the information around UAN, such as member id, mobile number, Aadhaar, PAN, name, date of birth and e-mail idâ¢	Select âGet Authorization PINâ to fetch the PIN on the registered mobile numberâ¢	Provide this PIN for verifying the request.â¢	Set up a username and password on the UAN portal for future use.Common Reasons for Allotment of Two UANsIf an employee changes his job, a new EPF account is set up by the new organisation. All existing EPF accounts are auto-linked with the UAN of the employee. Hence, there are high chances that a new UAN is allotted to the employee at the time of moving between jobs. There could be multiple reasons for allotment of new UAN. Listed here are some of the common reasons:â¢	In case an employee has not disclosed his previous UAN â In case an employee changes his job, he must make sure to disclose his existing UAN and EPF account number (Member ID) to the new employer. In absence of disclosure of this information, the employer may open a fresh PF account along with a new UAN.â¢	Non-disclosure of âDate of Exitâ by the previous employer â During the process of EPF transfer to the new employer, the old employer must mention the date of exit in the ECR (Electronic Challan and Return). In case of the absence of this information promptly, the new organisation may allot a new UAN to the employee.Consequences of Holding Two UANsTwo active UANs is not permitted by law and is against the rules. A member must have only one UAN with all the EPF accounts linked to it. EPF accounts cannot be transferred among employees. However, an employee who has two UANs can request for his EPF account to be transferred from one UAN to another and ask his previous UAN to be closed. Thus, an EPF account linked with one UAN will have to be compulsorily transferred to another EPF account linked with a separate UAN.What Should an Employee Do?In recent years, there have been multiple cases of employees assigning different UANs (Universal Account Number) to employees. According to EPF rules, an individual should have only one UAN at any given point of time. The employeeâs EPF account must be linked to his UAN. In case he/she has been assigned two UANs, the previous one must be deactivated at the earliest.Two Methods to Merge Two UAN EPF AccountsEmployees who have been incorrectly allotted two UANs must get one of them deactivated (normally, the previous one). There are two ways of getting the UAN deactivated and the EPF account transferred to the correct and active UAN. Mentioned below are the two commonly used methods:Method 1â¢	Reach out to your employer or EPFO and report the issue at the earliestâ¢	You can write an email to[emailÂ protected]stating about your current and previous UANâ¢	EPFO will begin verification on the issue once it gets notified about the issueâ¢	Your previous UAN is then blocked and the existing UAN remains activeâ¢	After this, you have to submit a claim for transferring the EPF account (linked with the blocked UAN) to the new active account.This process can be time-consuming and the general resolution rate is said to be very low. Thus, EPFO has set up a new procedure which is expected to make things easier for a member. It will especially be helpful while merging two UANs and transferring EPF easily. Here is the new method which can be used by an employee with two UANs:Method 2â¢	After thorough identification, old UAN will be deactivated by EPFO once the transfer of the EPF to the new UAN is completeâ¢	Thus, the old UANs will be blocked automatically and an employeeâs previous member ID will be linked to the new or existing UANâ¢	SMS notification is sent for the deactivation to the employeeâs registered mobile numberâ¢	If the employee has been unable to activate his new UAN, he will be notified to activate it at the earliest to receive the status update of the accountâ¢	There could be instances where the employee gets PF arrears from the previous employer. In such situations, the arrear is credited to the new PF account which is linked with the new UAN.Advantages of UAN for EmployeesMinimum Employer Involvement in PF withdrawals:  With the presence of UAN, the employer involvement is significantly reduced since the PF accumulation from the old organization is auto-transferred to the new PF account after completion of KYC verification.No Need for Fund Transfer: An employee must furnish his UAN details and KYC to the new employer for transferring the old PF balance to the new PF account post verification.Manage via SMS Alerts: Employees will receive SMS as soon as a contribution is made by the employer towards PF. This is provided, the employee has registered on the UAN portal.How to use UAN for PF Transfer?The Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) constantly takes several measures to make the operation of EPF accounts easier for both the employer and employees. To keep up with the technological advancements, EPFO is constantly striving towards streamlining of processes about online EPF. This is especially applicable to PF transfer and withdrawal of PF which are considered to be tedious and time-consuming processes.EPFO introduced Universal Account Number (UAN), which is the blanket number for multiple Member Ids given to an individual by various employers. UAN allows the linking of multiple EPF Accounts (Member Id) provided to a single EPF member. It offers a range of services such as dynamically updated UAN card, updated PF passbook including all transfer-in details, facility to link previous membersâ ID with present ID, monthly SMS regarding credit of contribution in PF account and facility for auto-triggering transfer request on change of employment.Till recently, PF transfer could be done online by going to the âOnline Transfer Claim Portalâ. However, with the introduction of UAN, the transfer process has been revised and shifted under the âunified portalâ. For online PF transfer, here are some of the important points to note:â¢	An EPF member must have activated his UAN on the UAN portal and the registered mobile number used for activation should be in an active state.â¢	The Bank account number and IFSC code of the employee's bank account must be updated against the UAN. Updated Aadhar number and PAN is not mandatory for PF transfer requests.â¢	The employer must approve the e-KYC for transfer to be executed.â¢	The previous/current employer must have digitally registered authorized signatories on EPFO portal.â¢	PF account number related to previous and current employment of an employee should be updated in EPFO database.â¢	Single transfer requests per member ID can be accepted.FAQs1. What if I have two UAN numbers? Does it impact my EPF balance or transfer in any way?Two different UAN numbers for one employee is not accepted and is against the rules. If you happen to change jobs and move between organizations, you must request for transfer of PF account at the earliest.2. What is the expected timeline for merging two EPF accounts?It normally takes around 20 days from the date of the request to transfer one EPF account to the other.3. Is Form 13 a prerequisite for UAN transfer?Employees working in the corporate sector are required to submit Form 13 for EPF transfer to their new PF account at the time of job change.4. How is Form 13 used?Form 13 is primarily used for the transfer of Provident Fund from one account to another. Employees have to submit this form to their employers, upon which, the latter have to verify and approve the details furnished.

question: Hi, My ex employer has made mistakes while submitting the PF amount. Though the EPS applicability was Yes for me, but while submitting the PF amount, my employer has mistakenly not deposited anything in to the pension head for three years. Now they have submitted the revised document with the local PF office. Its been months. But every time i check the status of the same with the PF office by raising grievance in the EPF system, it is still not done. I am looking to withdraw my PF. But i am not able to do the same due to this mistake, I don't know what to to do expedite the same and withdraw my PF.( Bhubaneswar, Orissa )
answer: Dear client,To address the issue of your ex-employer's mistakes in submitting the Provident Fund (PF) contributions legally these measures can be taken-1. Review Employment RecordsExamine Employment Contract: Check your employment contract and any communication regarding your PF contributions and eligibility for the Employee Pension Scheme (EPS).Collect Evidence: Gather documents that demonstrate your employment duration, the amount deducted for PF, and any correspondence regarding the contributions.2. Formal Communication with Ex-EmployerSend a Legal Notice: Draft a formal letter or legal notice to your ex-employer. The notice should outline:The discrepancies in the PF contributions.The legal obligation of the employer to remit contributions accurately.A request for immediate correction and confirmation of the revised submissions to the PF office.Set a Deadline: Specify a reasonable deadline for the employer to resolve the issue to avoid further legal action.3. Grievance with EPFOFile a Grievance: Utilize the EPFO grievance management system to file a formal complaint regarding the non-deposit of EPS contributions. Clearly state:The nature of the complaint.Reference any previous grievance tickets raised and their status.Follow Up: Persistently follow up with the EPFO through the grievance portal and, if possible, visit the local PF office to escalate the matter.4. RTI ApplicationFile an RTI Application: If the EPFO does not respond satisfactorily, file a Right to Information (RTI) application requesting information on:The status of your grievance.Details regarding the revision submitted by your employer.Timelines for resolution.Legal Provisions: The RTI Act empowers you to seek information, and the EPFO is obliged to respond within 30 days.5. Withdrawal ApplicationSubmit Withdrawal Application: You can submit your PF withdrawal application despite the discrepancies. Ensure that you:Complete the withdrawal form accurately.Attach all relevant documents, including your previous employment details and proof of contributions.Request for Processing: In your application, mention the issue with EPS contributions and request that the withdrawal be processed without delay.6. Seek Legal RemedyConsult a Lawyer: If your ex-employer fails to respond or rectify the issue, consult a lawyer specializing in labor law. They can:Advise on further legal action, such as filing a petition in the labor court or consumer forum against your ex-employer for failing to meet statutory obligations.Assist in drafting any additional legal notices required.7. Monitor ProgressDocument Everything: Keep a comprehensive record of all communications, grievances, applications, and responses related to your PF account. This documentation will be crucial if legal action is required.Check Status Regularly: Regularly check the status of your grievance with the EPFO and maintain contact with your ex-employer.8. Potential Legal ProceedingsFile a Case: If the situation does not resolve, your lawyer may recommend filing a case against the employer for recovery of dues and seeking compliance with PF regulations. This could involve:Filing a complaint under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, for non-compliance.Seeking damages for any financial loss suffered due to the employer's negligence.

question: I joined the company on 1st November 2022 and have been employedâtwo years of bond which is completed on 31 October 2024. I have given my resignation on 31 August 2024. question: I was working in Tech Mahindra, Mumbai and I left it in the month of July 24, in my FFS they are mentioning that FFS is negative because PAN-AADHAAR not being linked together and govt has imposed penalty on them of Rs.  1,04,859/-  which they are now asking me to re-pay this amount to them. answer: Dear Client,In your situation regarding the penalty imposed by Tech Mahindra related to the non-linking of your PAN and Aadhaar, here are a few points to consider:Typically, the liability to pay any penalties imposed on the employer due to regulatory issues (like the non-linking of PAN and Aadhaar) is the responsibility of the company, not the individual employee. The employer is responsible for ensuring compliance with such requirements.Unless there was a specific agreement or clause in your employment contract stating that you would be liable for such penalties, it is unlikely that you are legally bound to repay this amount.Review your employment contract and any company policies regarding payroll, penalties, and tax compliance. question:
I have resigned From Tata Projects limited just after my 3 months service with 10 days short notice out of 90 days. At time of full and final settlement company not considered my served notice period of 10 days and presented a demand of Rs.31815 however i paid this amount.In recepit of my service certificate it is pointed that the reason behind leave the organization mentioned was termination.

What steps i have to take.( Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,For breach of contract of employment on the part of an employee, a company can take action against the employee post-resignation, but cannot mention the reason behind the cessation of employment as termination especially when the employee meets the demands of the company towards breach of contract. The word termination in your relieving letter post-resignation is itself a stigma that adversely affects your future career unless you challenge and nullify that stigma. When you meet the demands of the company, it may be unprofessional and unconstitutional on the part of the Company to issue you a relieving letter placing a stigma on it that infringes a person's fundamental right to life as guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. Termination or retrenchment other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman serving a legal notice to the Company can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned within one year from termination for adjudication seeking retrenchment compensation under Section 33C(2) of the I D Act provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. To restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. Otherwise, in case you are holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, you have to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

question: In the promotion policy of organisation, there is eligibility criteria of promotion to next grade after 4 years. As me and my number of colleagues joined on same duration, same criteria applicable for them. Now even after completion of 5 years, we are not getting promoted. And there is no restriction of vacancies as the work-profile is same. (Also we are playing same roles and responsibilities which taken by already promoted employees to next grade).( Nagpur, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Regardless of the sector or class of establishments either public or private, the recruitment, promotion, placement, and rationalization of manpower is processed following its standing HR policy and promotion or degradation of manpower is also a prerogative of the management of an establishment. Any complaint or allegation over malpractice or unfair practice against the HR Policy of an establishment shall not be entertained by a Tribunal or Court unless the alleged malpractice or unfairness in HR policy and practice appears on the face of the record. So, it is a very difficult and cumbersome exercise to prove such an allegation against an establishment before the Tribunals/Courts.  Only in case of deviation/ discrimination/mala fide in the policy or rules, if it appears on the face of the record, the Tribunal/High Court may entertain an application or appeal challenging the HR Policy violating the well-established policy of the organization. Otherwise, an application or appeal may be rejected at the stage of admission for lack of merit. So, if you are confident in the merit behind your claim/grievance, you can escalate your grievance before the appropriate authority(Labour Commissioner), State or Central Govt. Labour Courts, SAT/CAT befitting your sector or class of employment for redressal of your grievance.

question:
I was working for a client company through a vendor company ( this company takes care of my Payroll ). Due to some issues I was dropped from my client project and my vendor company asked me to relieve immediately. They didn't ask me to serve notice period in email / call. I have informed them that I was ready to serve notice which they denied. They demanded me to pay 50k which is the travel advance amount I have used for clients' project travel. I was continuously following them up to relieve me for more than a month through email & calls. HR didn't respond to my calls later. Later my email got blocked. At the same time I became bedridden due to pregnancy. They asked me to come to office to talk about relieving formalities. I mentioned my condition clearly and requested them to talk over phone (anyways they were not interested in me serving notice period). No response for email / call from HR. I left it due to my health condition for a while. Now, when I ask them for my relieving documents, they are demanding me to pay three months salary and accusing me of not serving notice which I was ready to. 
What should I do in this case? I have mentioned clearly I was ready to serve in other projects but they terminated me and also denied me to serve any notice.
Now they are blocking my experience letter / relieving documents.
The company didn't pay any compensation to me for immediate termination. Can someone help me how to proceed on this further?( Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,In your situation, where you were ready to serve the notice period but the vendor company denied it and is now demanding three months' salary while blocking your relieving documents and experience letter, you have a strong case to seek redress. Hereâs how you can proceed:Gather all written communications (emails, messages) where you informed the company about your willingness to serve the notice period and where they denied it.Keep records of the email conversations where they asked you to clear the travel advance.Document any medical proof (doctor's notes, hospital records) regarding your pregnancy and bedridden condition, as this is critical in justifying why you couldn't visit their office in person.Draft a formal legal notice to the vendor company. In this notice, state the facts clearly:You were terminated without notice and were willing to serve the notice period.The company did not respond to your attempts to resolve the matter.They are withholding your relieving documents and experience letter without proper justification.You have no liability to pay three monthsâ salary, as you were ready to serve the notice, but the company terminated your employment.Request them to provide the relieving documents and experience letter within a specific time frame (e.g., 15 days) or face legal consequences.A legal notice from an advocate may prompt them to resolve the issue without court intervention.If the company does not respond to your legal notice, you can file a complaint with the Labour Commissioner in your area. The Labour Department can help you mediate with the company and ensure you receive your documents and any unpaid dues (such as compensation for wrongful termination).Visit the local Labour Department office in Tiruchirappalli.Provide all necessary documents (appointment letter, email conversations, etc.) and explain the issue.The Labour Department will call for a conciliation meeting between you and the employer to resolve the issue.If the matter still doesnât get resolved through the Labour Department, you can file a civil suit for:Wrongful termination, since they terminated you without allowing you to serve the notice period.Damages for mental stress and blocking your career progression due to withholding of documents.You can also claim compensation for the immediate termination without any settlement.To avoid complications, you may consider clearing the travel advance of â¹50,000 (if it was indeed an advance provided to you), as it is a separate issue from your termination.If thereâs any employment contract or offer letter that includes clauses about termination, notice period, or relieving procedures, review it thoroughly to see if the vendor company has violated any terms. Use these points to strengthen your case.Regards

question: My employer asked me to resign, I'll tried to convince them, but they are not accepted. I'll send my resignation via e-mail, they accepted immediately and don't agreed to serve the notice period and gave the Last Working Day within less than a week. Can I demand any compensation from them for the unserved notice period?( Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,In your situation, since your employer has asked you to resign and has not allowed you to serve your notice period, there are certain legal principles and remedies you can explore under Indian labor laws and your employment contract. Hereâs a step-by-step breakdown of what you can do:Review Your Employment Contract, check your employment contract to understand the notice period clause. Most employment contracts specify a notice period (usually 1-3 months), during which either the employer or employee must serve notice before resignation or termination.The contract may also mention compensation in lieu of notice if the notice period is not served by either party.If your employer asked you to resign and did not allow you to serve your notice period, they are typically obligated to compensate you for the unserved portion of the notice period, unless the contract specifies otherwise.For instance, if your contract mentions a one-month notice period and they are letting you go within a week, they should ideally pay you for the remaining days or weeks of the notice period.If your employer is terminating your services early without allowing you to serve the agreed notice period, you can send an official demand for compensation in writing, either via email or a formal letter.In your letter, reference the terms of your employment contract regarding notice period obligations and request compensation for the period they are not allowing you to serve.Under the Shops and Establishments Act, applicable in Andhra Pradesh and most other states, employees are generally entitled to a notice period or pay in lieu of notice if they are asked to leave early.If your employer has violated these provisions by not allowing you to serve the notice period, you may have grounds to demand compensation for the same.If your employer refuses to provide compensation, you can approach the Labour Commissionerâs office in Vijayawada to file a formal complaint regarding unfair termination practices and demand compensation for the unserved notice period.The Labour Commissioner will likely mediate between you and your employer to resolve the issue.If you were forced to resign (i.e., the resignation was not voluntary), you may have grounds to claim wrongful termination. In such cases, you could claim compensation not only for the unserved notice period but potentially for wrongful termination as well.Steps to Follow:Draft an email, letter or a legal notice clearly stating your demand for compensation for the unserved notice period, citing your employment contract and legal rights under the Shops and Establishments Act.If your employer refuses, you can file a formal complaint with the Labour Department in Vijayawada or consult a labor lawyer to take further action.Regards

question: How can I recover my cash lost by online job scammer( Alappuzha, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal(NCCRP) is an initiative of the Government of India to facilitate victims/complainants to report cybercrime including online job scams or complaints. Once a cybercrime scam or fraudulent transaction is reported online to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal(NCCRP), on the instruction of the Cyber Crime Cell, the investigating team starts the routine process of investigation immediately. You have to wait for the completion of the investigation of the scam by the investigating agency to get back the money lost in the scam. The length of time it takes to investigate a cybercrime can vary greatly depending on the complexity of the case, the resources available to the investigators, and the cooperation of the victim. Please keep in regular contact with the Cyber cell and the Bank and extend your full cooperation in the investigation to resolve the matter at the earliest. You may consult with a cyber crime expert or an Advocate handling cyber laws for further guidance and suitable steps.

question: I am an intern and frequently i've been getting my payment extremely late due to which my monthly budget schedule shakes up. I continuously msg for updates of payment but get no reply. Is it possible to take any legal action regarding this?( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Internships are often unpaid and may not lead to a full-time job. Stipends are provided to those ineligible to receive a regular salary or wage in return for their services. Researchers, graduate students, clergy, interns and apprentices are common recipients. However, internships remain an unregulated sector and as a result, in most cases, interns are not legally entitled to minimum wages or modes of legal redressal that otherwise apply to permanent employees. So considering the status of interns, in the absence of a specific stipulation in your offer letter, your claim for payment of a stipend in the scheduled time may not be upheld even through litigation.

question:

My father worked in a co-op housing society as a guard  from the last 9-10 years.
In august month my father was on approved leave with application . but 3-4 days late due to illnesses . so society is not ready to continue to keep him on job as before .
Housing society terminates my father without notice and the secretary is saying you're not eligible for any gratuity  notice salary .
How will I get the full and final amount from This housing society?( Mumbai, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,If your father was terminated without notice from his job as a security guard after serving for 9-10 years, he has legal rights to claim various benefits, including notice salary, gratuity, and other dues. Here are the steps you can take to get the full and final settlement from the housing society:Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, an employee who has worked for at least 5 years is eligible for gratuity. Since your father worked for 9-10 years, he is legally entitled to receive gratuity.Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, your father is entitled to a notice period before termination. If no notice was given, he is entitled to receive compensation in lieu of the notice period (usually one monthâs salary).Any unpaid salary for the days he worked, earned leave, and other benefits like provident fund (if applicable) should be part of the full and final settlement.Steps to Take:Send a Formal Legal Notice:Draft a legal notice to the housing society, specifically addressing the secretary and the management committee.In the notice, mention the number of years your father worked, the fact that he was on approved leave and returned late due to illness, the societyâs failure to provide notice or compensation for the termination.Demand gratuity payment as per the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, compensation for the notice period (or salary in lieu of notice), unpaid salary, leave encashment, and other dues.Give a reasonable deadline (15-30 days) for the society to make the payment.Contact the Labour Commissionerâs Office:If the society doesnât respond or refuses to settle the dues, file a complaint with the Labour Commissionerâs Office in Mumbai.The Labour Department will summon the society for conciliation, and they will try to mediate the dispute.In the complaint, include all details such as the years of service, the nature of the termination, and the benefits your father is entitled to (gratuity, notice pay, etc.).File a Gratuity Claim:If the housing society refuses to pay the gratuity, you can file a claim with the Controlling Authority for Payment of Gratuity.You can download and submit Form I under the Payment of Gratuity Act, which is
