mediation fails or the Labour Commissioner is unable to resolve the issue, you can escalate the matter by filing a case in the Labour Court.A lawyer specializing in labor disputes will help in drafting the petition and represent your fatherâs case.The court can order the society to pay the gratuity, notice period compensation, and other unpaid dues.Keep any appointment letter, service certificate, or proof of employment with the society.The approved leave application or any proof that the leave was sanctioned.Proof of salary and any deductions (if available).Medical documents: Medical certificates that show the illness for the delay in returning from leave.If a formal termination letter was issued, keep it as part of your evidence.If the societyâs termination of your fatherâs job was done without following the due process (i.e., no proper investigation or opportunity for a hearing), you can also claim compensation for wrongful termination under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The court may order additional compensation based on the wrongful termination.If your father was part of any union or workerâs association, you can approach them for additional support. They may help in filing complaints or pursuing the case.Regards

question: Sir, I have mailed my resignation letter to my HR on 19th august and joined another company on 20 th august. But still my previous employer paid me full salary for august. On 9 September I contacted my HR regarding this issue. They said your last working day would be on 3 September as my immediate manager accepted my separation from organization on 3 September.  So in this case what should I do.( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Before joining another Company you are required to tender your resignation and to obtain a relieving letter from the earlier company serving the notice period as per the terms of employment that eventually caused the overlapping of service. The overlapping in service in respect of previous and present establishment and any anomaly or discrepancy in EPF records of any registered member may be a ground for future dispute. When your EPF record shows an anomaly in the joining and exit date in both the previous and present Company which is contradictory, then until and unless those anomalies are rectified by the concerned employers, PF records will show overlapping or dual employment. A joint declaration form is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. An employee cannot update the service history. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database, he should contact their present or previous employers and get it corrected. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly arising out of the date of appointment and date of discharge in EPF records. An individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). Once you succeed in wiping out the stigma of dual employment from your EPF records with the cooperation of your previous and present employer, your scope of employment with other companies will be restored with clean employment records. In case of non-cooperation from both previous and current employers which amounted to unfair labour practice, you may bring the matter to the notice of the Regopmal PF Commissioner and the concerned Labour Commissioner or Asst. Labour Commissioner/LEO/Chief Inspector(Shops and Establishment) for a resolution in the matter.

question: How to remove or change this DOE of previous employers ?( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,A joint declaration form(JDF) is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer jointly sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts by default. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of dual employment/overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly/discrepancy arising out of date of appointment and date of exit of an employee in EPF records. For lack of cooperation from the employers who are duty-bound to correct the records of member employees in EPF records, an individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). or filing a complaint offline in the office of the Regional PF Commissioner concerned. If the complaint is not resolved even on receipt of JDF, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief yields from the office of the PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief.

question: can i re-join my job after maternity leave (approx one year leave).i sent the letter to the department after one year of maternity leave dt.20/03/2017 but till date they have not given any approval to join( Jamshedpur, Jharkhand )
answer: Dear Client,If you are facing issues rejoining your job after maternity leave and the department has not provided approval for your return, there are a few important legal and procedural steps you can take to address this situation. Here's a breakdown of your rights and the steps you should follow:Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, every woman is entitled to 26 weeks of maternity leave (increased from 12 weeks as of 2017).You are legally allowed to rejoin your job after your maternity leave.If you have taken an extended leave beyond the statutory period (such as one year), this could fall under either earned leave, unpaid leave, or medical leave, depending on your organizationâs policies.Review your organization's leave policy. If you have taken an extended period of leave beyond the statutory maternity leave (like an additional 6 months or more), it is important to check whether this was approved or whether it was unpaid leave or medical leave.If the leave was properly communicated and accepted by the employer, they should allow you to rejoin.Since you have already sent a letter requesting rejoining (dated 20/03/2017), you should send a follow-up letter or email to the department, seeking a written response regarding the delay in allowing you to rejoin.Attach the previous letter you sent, and make sure to keep copies of all communication for record purposes.If there is no response from the department despite repeated follow-ups, you may need to send a formal legal notice through a lawyer, demanding approval for rejoining and clarification on why your request is being delayed.In the legal notice, mention the Maternity Benefit Act and your rights as an employee to return after maternity leave.If the immediate department is not responding, you can escalate the matter to higher authorities within your organization, such as the HR department, higher management, or even the Ministry of Labour, depending on whether you work for a public or private organization.If the department refuses to allow you to rejoin or if you are being denied your rights under the Maternity Benefit Act, you can file a complaint with the Labour Court or the Labour Commissioner in your area.They will look into your case and can intervene to ensure that your rights as a returning mother are upheld.If your employer fails to reinstate you after your approved leave or does not respond for an extended period, you may be entitled to claim back wages for the period after your maternity leave, especially if you were willing to rejoin but were denied.It might be beneficial to consult an Advocate who can assist you in drafting the necessary legal notice or filing a complaint in the labour court.Regards

question:

In the first phase, the cutoff for UR candidates was set at 800 (with 13 seats), while the cutoff for EWS candidates was 720 (with 3 seats). The scores of the EWS candidates who were selected were 781, 753, and 720.

In the second phase, the cutoff for UR candidates dropped to 780, but no new EWS candidates were selected, meaning there was no upgradation among the EWS candidates selected in the first phase.

By the fourth phase, the UR cutoff had further decreased to 690, while the EWS cutoff remained at 720.

My question is: Why were the EWS candidates not upgraded when UR candidates did not join in the earlier phases? Shouldnât the EWS candidates have been promoted to UR status, allowing the next candidates in line to be selected for the EWS category?( Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,Your question relates to the allocation and upgradation process in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) that recruit through GATE scores and whether candidates from the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) category should be upgraded to the Unreserved (UR) category when the UR cutoff drops.EWS candidates are eligible to compete both in their reserved category (EWS) and in the unreserved (UR) category, provided they meet the UR cutoff.In your case, the EWS cutoff was 720, while the UR cutoff started at 800 in the first phase and then gradually dropped to 780 and later to question: I have been working in a corporate firm since 2 years and I was scheduled to have a Microsoft teams video call couple of days before. If your company has an ethics committee, you can also submit your complaint there for investigation.As for legal considerations, asking for live access to your bank account during a call is a significant breach of privacy. question: My sons current employer have his original certificates in custody and are demanding 2 lakhs to return them of he wants to quit. They have taken undertaki gduring his joining. Is it legally correct? What steps do we take now?( Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of Employment bonds can be challenged based on Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract) and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. Further, withholding your original documents on the cessation of the relationship between an employer and employee post-resignation to recover the bond value amounts to unfair labour practice on the part of the employer in view of the aforesaid provision of the Indian Contract Act,1872.  So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishment to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit before the Civil Court for desired relief in the matter.

question: My employer repeatedly demands original marksheet of class 10th. The company is not registered and they deduct 10% tds from everyone's salary. At the time of salary they didn't give salary slip to any employee.( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,An employer can neither demand an original mark sheet from a candidate/employee nor keep it in their custody as a token of security. A self-attested Xerox copy of the mark sheet or a copy attested by any gazetted officer of the state or central government is sufficient to meet any purpose. A salary slip contains a detailed break-up of an employee's salary from gross salary to the take-home salary with deductions. A salary slip is a legal right of an employee in a company and if the company refuses to provide a salary slip or pay slip, it amounts to unfair labour practice. TAN (Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number) is mandatory for any company, firm, or individual, who deducts or collects tax at source, on behalf of the Income Tax Department. As per Section 192 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, TDS is required to be deducted from all the monetary amounts paid by the employer under the head 'Salary' to his employee if the amount so paid exceeds the threshold exemption limit of Income. Form 16 is a TDS certificate issued by the employer as proof of tax deducted from the employee's salary income. It serves as proof that tax has been deducted at source from the employee's salary income and deposited with the government. It is essential for filing income tax returns. A taxpayer can download Form 16 from TRACES (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System) an online website of the Income Tax Department of India. As explained in the query, all the actions of the company appear to be arbitrary and unfair labour practices as defined under Section 2(ra) of the Industrial Dispute Act. So, you can make a complaint/grievance against the company before the concerned Labour Commissioner of the State Govt. who is the appropriate authority under the Payment of Wages Act, Shops and Establishments Act and Minimum Wages Act to resolve the dispute.

There is no bar to the immediate superior officer holding an inquiry but, as a rule, the person who undertakes this task should not be suspected of any bias in such cases. question: I was working as a mechanical fitter in cement factory which is a private sector company and last month i got retired by the company at the age of 58. I want to claim my 2 years of salary from the company because in my knowledge supreme court has said the retirement age for the private company employee will be 60. Please guide me for the same.( Satna, Madhya Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,There is no official retirement age in private sector companies. However, employees can retire at the age of 58 or 60 based on their employment contract, employerâs policies, or mutual agreement with the employer. The retirement age for private company employees who belong to I T Sector, Multinational Companies MNC, and Banking Sector is 60 years, and for Marketing Sectors is between 58 to 60 years. Clause 3 of Schedule - I B of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 states that the age of retirement or superannuation of a workman shall be as may be agreed upon between the employer and the workman under an agreement or as specified in a settlement or award which is binding on both the workman and the employer. Where there is no such agreed age, retirement or superannuation shall be on completion of 58 years of age by the workman. In G.M. Talang and Ors. V/s Shaw Wallace and Co. and Anr., as decided on 24.03.1964 the Honâble Supreme Court of India held that after taking into consideration the views of the earlier Committees and Commissions including those of the Second Pay Commission the report of which has been released recently, we feel that the retirement age for workmen in all industries should be fixed at 60. Accordingly, the norm for retirement age is fixed at 60. The above judgment was upheld in Tej Bahadur Ram V/s State of U.P. and Ors, arising from SLP(C)No.18692/2005. In the case of employees who are not workmen, the age of retirement is decided by the service rules determined by the Company and accepted by the Company. In the case of managerial cadre or executives, the age of retirement is determined by the contract of employment/employment agreement. So, if there is no employment contract, employerâs policies, mutual agreement with the employer, or a settlement award governing the age of retirement, you may take up the matter with the Company as well as the Labour Commissioner or, Inspector of Factories for the review of your retirement age, otherwise, the provision of Clause 3 of Schedule - I B of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 prescribed fixing the age of retirement at 58 shall prevail.

An employee could be entitled to get 'payment in lieu of notice'. This means the employer stops work straight away but still gets paid for their notice period. Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Under Chapters V-A & V-B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, for retrenchment of a workman of an industrial establishment employing below 100 workmen, an employer has to pay one month's notice or wages in lieu of notice, compensation of Fifteen days average pay for every completed year of service. 6 months and above to be treated as one year and service of Notice to the appropriate Government(Labour Commissioner) informing retrenchment of workmen. In that scenario, serving a legal notice to the Company, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the dispute failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication of the dispute provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. To restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. question:
Hi,
I hope you're doing well. I have a question regarding gratuity eligibility:
I have worked with a private organization for around 16 years. However, for the past 15 years, the salary payments were made in cash, and I only have a salary statement for the last year. The company is relatively small, with about 15 to 20 employees.
I joined as a fresher in 2003, so my documentation is limited that time and the i have only salary statement for the last year. Given this situation, am I still eligible for a gratuity amount?
Any guidance or advice would be greatly appreciated!( Chennai, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,An organization/establishment with a workforce of 10 individuals and above is liable to pay gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act 1972. A gratuity must be paid to an employee upon cessation of employment if he or she has rendered continuous service for five years or more, according to Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act of 1972. Section 4(2) of the Act provides that for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of 6 months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the prescribed rates. The Gratuity Benefits are calculated using the following formula:-(15/26) multiplied by (No of Completed Years on Exit) multiplied by (Terminal Wages/Salary). Under Rule 7(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Rules, 1972, an employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Act, or any person authorized, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, within thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form 'I' to the employer who is duty bound to disburse the gratuity within 30 days of cessation of employment of employee or claim made by an employee. After 30 days, the employer has to pay you not only the gratuity amount but also the simple interest accrued for the delay in payment of the gratuity. Company is practising malfunction against me. 
What should i say to the civil judge on my hearing, Kindly make a list with the proper acts and Rule.

A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of Employment bonds can be challenged based on Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. The action of the Company prima facie appears to be victimization and unfair labour practice. When you quit the company on the last day of your internship that does not attract any hefty amount of compensation as claimed by the Company, so, let them prove their actual loss or damages caused for tendering resignation by an intern on the LWD of the internship. answer: Dear Client,Background verification(BGV) check is a process many organizations carry out in order to verify the information provided by the candidate during hiring. Verification of EPFO records through UAN is a critical process for conducting employee background checks because it allows employers to confirm that their employees are not using false or stolen identities to gain employment. In case of a negative background verification check an employer can even reject or terminate the employment of the candidate.  Organizations with more than 20 employees must register under the EPF scheme and EPF registration with EPFO is mandatory for salaried employees with an income of up to â¹ 15,000 per month. But, when your previous employer has no registration under the EPF scheme of EPF & MP Act 1952, they cannot deduct contributions from an employee towards PF and in the absence of registration, there is no scope to generate  UAN for the employees of that establishment. Despite eligibility, if your previous employer did not register the establishment under the EPF Scheme, then on complaint to PF Commissioner, they may face prosecution and penalties and may be directed to register the organization under the EFP Scheme, but such registration shall have no retrospective effect and will not serve any purpose in your case. So, there is no feasible way to resolve the issue save and except your convincing ability to satisfy with the situation but, that also depends upon the discretion of your prospective employer.

question: Hello sir, I am a person with benchmark disability. I have locomotor disability of 62% as mentioned in my UDID card. They alloted me a temporary card which is valid for 5 years from the date of issue. Am I eligible for SSC or central government jobs? In the job notification and online form fillup, it's only mentioned as  persons above 40% disability are eligible. I am confused that my certificate which is temporarily valid for 5 years is eligible or not? Sir, please clear my confusion if possible. Thank you Sir.( Cachar, Assam )
answer: Dear Client,The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act was enacted in the year 2016 and came into force on 19th April 2017. Individuals having 40% or more disability can apply for a disability certificate, provided their disability falls under the categories specified under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Issue of A Unique Disability Identity(UDID) card to a PWD is an initiative by the Government of India with a view of creating a National Database for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs). The UDID card and Disability Certificate have two types of validity- Permanent UDID card and Temporary UDID Card. Permanent UDID: The competent medical authority issues a Permanent UDID Card considering there is no progress or regress in the disability of a PwD. Temporary UDID: The competent medical authority issues a Temporary UDID Card considering there is progress or a regress in the disability of a PwD. A disability certificate remains valid for lifelong in case of a permanent disability. However, for temporary disabilities, the certificate/ID card remains valid for a period of five years. It has to be renewed once in five years subject to the medical examination of the disabled person. So, regardless of the nature and class of PWD and UDID Certificate, a candidate having 40% or more disability can apply for SSC or central government jobs during the period of validity of the UDID Certificate.

question: After serving the organisation for more than 33 years, my payment of gratuity was made after more than one year, and that too in instalments, spread over six months. answer: Dear Client,If your gratuity payment has been delayed for over a year and is being paid in installments, you can have a legal justification to ask for an interest on the delayed gratuity. As for the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, employers are supposed to pay simple interest from when gratuity becomes payable to when it is paid. This interest is not an option since it is required by the court order and therefore cannot be considered as optional. If the employer fails to pay the interest and your matter is in the Deputy Labour Commissioner then it is advisable to take the next step. You can report to the Controlling Authority under the Payment of Gratuity Act for the recovery of gratuity with interest. However, if the authority does not act in your favour, then you can seek remedy from the Labour Court. This means that if the delay is as a result of bureaucratic factors, one may also be charged interest at the current rates of General Provident Fund. To assist your claim, you should keep records of communications with your employer and the Deputy Labour Commissioner.Hope this advice helps in solving your query.

Your remedy lies in Civil Court. Before filing the suit you need to serve a legal notice to the management making a demand for pay in lieu of notice post illegal termination. A Suit for recovery of money is a civil relief and acts as an effective remedy to recover money from the defendant. The suit can be filed under Order IV of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 (CPC). It is a summary suit (Order 37, Code of Civil Procedure) that offers speedy disposal of the suit as here the defendant is not required to defend as a matter of right. A money recovery suit must be filed within three years from the date of cause of action. Any document, message, contract, mail, telephonic conversation, or post can serve as proper evidence in the Court to prove the claim or demand. As per Sec. 20 of the Civil Procedure Code a suit for recovery of money may be instituted either at (i) where the cause of action wholly or partly arose or (ii) where the defendant resides or carries on business or (iii) where there are two or more defendants, where one of them resides or carries on business. In this context, the following citation/judgments of the High Court/Supreme Court may be referred to. Prayag Deb vs. Rama Roy, AIR 1977 CAL I (FB) of Calcutta High Court and Milkhiram India (P) Ltd. vs. Chamanlal Bros., AIR 1965 SC 1698 of Supreme Court.

If you are associated with discharge, where employees are let go off work due to incompetence among other factors while the latter is associated with termination on grounds of poor performance or engaging in unlawful activities. If you felt that you were going to be fired, this could be challenged on this ground alone. Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 employees can be dismissed without any notice and without payment of notice wages unless he has been dismissed for misconduct. The Supreme Court has said that the final settlements, including notice pay, should be made on the last working day in various judicial pronouncements. Omission of this payment may also be deemed as a violation of the employeeâs rights.Hope you find this advice beneficial.

question: My wife Tanuja Dutta had passed SCHOOL SERVICE COMMISSION (IX XII) TET IN 2016. AFTER 7TH COUNSELING SHE DID NOT GET SELECTED. SHE IS IN THE WAITING LIST 27 IN FEMALE OBC . question:
I resigned from my company, and during my notice period, the company got acquired. By the time I completed my notice period, I had 15 days of leave remaining. The new company is now saying they will only encash the leave up until June (6 months) because the acquisition happened in July. It comes out toe be 9 days of leave. I also want to mention that I didn't join the new company neither signed any contract with them
Is this legally correct under Indian labor laws, or should all my accrued leave be encashed regardless of the acquisition date?( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,As per the Indian labor laws, under the Factories Act, 1948, employees are entitled to encash their accrued leave when they leave the company. This right to leave encashment is typically independent of whether the company has been acquired or not.  When a company gets acquired, the new company inherits the liabilities and obligations of the old company, including accrued leave of employees. If you had 15 days of accrued leave at the time of your resignation, you are entitled to encash the entire amount. If you completed your notice period and did not enter into any contract with the new company, your leave encashment should ideally be based on the policies of the old company up until the last day of your employment. Report the issue with the HR department, give them a formal written request for leave encashment. If they still refuse, approach the labor commissioner. We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question: Recently I have given interview in private collage and they have taken my original documents and I have got another opportunity outside now and that collage is not ready to return my documents. What is the solution for this( Dharwad, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,In the case of Jayakumar v. Krishnaswamy Iyyengar, it was held that party cannot be permitted to gain advantage by withholding vital document. Write a formal letter or email to the college administration, specifically addressing it to the principal or the HR department. Clearly state that you have decided not to join the college and request the immediate return of your original documents. Mention that withholding the documents without valid reason is illegal. Visit the college in person and request your documents directly from the administrative office or HR department. If the college is affiliated with a university or educational board, you can file a complaint with the university's grievance cell. Inform them about the collegeâs refusal to return your documents, and they may intervene on your behalf. As a last resort, send a legal notice to the college, demanding the immediate return of your original documents. If the college still refuses to return your documents after you have sent a legal notice, you can file a police complaint. Also you may have to file a case in a civil court seeking the return of your documents. We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question: I am working in my current organisation for 3 years. As per my appointment letter notice period was 90 days. But i already drop a resignation notice on 23.07.2024 to serve a notice period of 60 days and pay remaining 30 days. So what I have to do in this scenario( Chennai, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,Send follow-up emails to your manager and HR, remind them of your resignation notice and your intent to serve a 60-day notice period. Mention your willingness to pay for the remaining 30 days, as per the terms of your appointment letter. Go through your employment contract to understand the exact terms regarding resignation, notice period, and the procedure for leaving. Ensure that you are complying with all the terms mentioned in the contract. If your manager is unresponsive, escalate the matter to the HR department. Request for a written confirmation of your resignation and the acceptance of your notice period from HR. Consult a lawyer and consider sending a legal notice to your current employer, stating that you have complied with the terms of your resignation and intend to leave on the specified date. We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question: I have signed a bond of 5 years in the company, I have completed one year. Now i have been put into PIP. If i get terminated or resign after the PIP period ends will i be liable to to pay the bond amount?( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,In case you have resigned voluntarily before completing the bond period, many agreements would require you to pay the bond amount as you are breaking the contract. Check the specific clauses related to resignation, termination, and PIP.  If the terms are ambiguous, it might be helpful to discuss with your HR department or consult a legal professional to understand your obligations. Though If the bond explicitly states that you owe the bond amount upon resignation, you might have to pay it even if you resign after PIP. However, the company's ability to enforce the bond in this case would depend on the specific terms and conditions We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question: My previous employer is making delay in issuing the Relieving letter, it has been 3 months thy are not responding to my mails, not my calls, what do i do? as important document it is, i am unable to join to different company( Dharwad, Karnataka )
answer: Dear client,If your previous employer is causing a hold up in granting you a relieving letter, you have some legal rights. First, Collect all the documents that would be useful namely, the appointment letter, the resignation letter, and the e-mails. Demand a formal written letter of the duration of employment, resignation submission, and unlawful retention of the letter citing section 22(c) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. If no response is received within the prescribed period then file a complaint to the Labor Commissionerâs office. Lastly, you can approach the Civil Court for a mandatory injunction for the purpose of getting the said relieving letter and all the other documents/salary that one has been denied.Hope you find this advice beneficial.

question: I have 3 days overlap issue in my service now I am changing to MNC company they have asked me for any Mail confirmation from my previous companies as changing in dates, they are not accepting this I need suggestion for this( Warangal, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,In India, it is legal to hold multiple jobs without breaching the law. Contact the HR departments of your previous companies and request for a formal clarification of the email or letter that acknowledges the overlap and provide the correct dates. If possible, write a self-declaration letter explaining the overlap, including the correct dates and write the reason for the overlap. Clearly communicate the problems you are facing in obtaining the required document. If the HR of your previous companies is uncooperative, escalate the matter to higher authority. question:
Company was asked for forced resignation suddenly that was unnoticed and without valid reason.. After resignation given Head HR it was accepted and released me immediately.. I have the copy of release and clearance form which mentions all assets and other belongings ,pending tasks handed over to concern person and verified also by concern person after it was signature by Head HR in my clearance form which is available with me.. After few days later suddenly Head HR asked me in mail to visit office for some pending tasks which after my last working day and after all clearance and resignation acceptance.. My question is ââââ-
1. Is it right for me to visit office after all my clearance and my last working day which my employment contract already has been ended??? Is it ethical as per legal? What should I do now?
2. Is it ethical to access companyâs documents, files , papers, data, SIM card ,assets after ending my employment contract??( Kolkata, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,Under section 27 of Indian Contract Act, 1872, Agreements restricting anyone from entering a profession, trade, service, or business are deemed invalid. Employment contracts are legally binding for both parties based on various terms and conditions. If thereâs a separation clause with the term âin lieu ofâ related to payment against the notice period, the employer cannot pressurize an employee to continue working. In the case of Sanjay Jain v. National Aviation Co. of India Ltd., (2019) 14 SCC 492, the Supreme Court stated that an employee cannot be forced to continue serving beyond the notice period unless stipulated in the employment terms. If the company is asking you to visit the office after your resignation has been accepted and processed, it is not legally binding for you to comply, especially since your official employment has ended. As your employment is officially over, you do not have any rights to access or use the company's documents, files, or other assets. If you do so, it would be considered unauthorized access, which may have negative legal consequences. Send a formal written mail or letter to the HR of the company stating that your employment contract has ended, all clearance and resignation acceptance are made and you are not obligated to return to work. We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question: Sir, in my offer it clearly states that unless I have been provided written confirmation I will be still in probation. But over the course of years, I have received increments and promotion. Now they say I need to serve 3 month notice instead of 1 month without any full and final payment and they have not paid for my previous month salary. Please advise( Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,Under The Payment of Wages Act, employer may, after obtaining the written authorization of the employed person, pay him the wages either be cheque or by crediting the wages in his bank account. Gather all the evidences of appointment letter, salary slips, promotion letter. Send a formal notice to your employer about your employment status including the unpaid salary. Communicate with HR and request a clear explanation of why they are enforcing a 3-month notice period, when the contract states a 1-month notice period. If HR ignores the matter, reach the higher authorities. Send an letter to HR and your manager, stating the amount due and the period it covers. If the company is not adhering to employment laws or your contract, you can file a complaint with the Labor Commissioner in your area. We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question: I was working with the  company from July-2023 to July-2024 (11 months 25 days), 18% of total CTC was as my variable pay.. i left the company and now company refusing for the variable pay stating after confirmation you are eligible to get the variable pay amount while in no where it is mentioned in the offer letter, Please suggest action can be taken against the company to get the variable pay which is part of my ctc( Mumbai, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,In case your former employer is reluctance to pay the variable pay which is 18% of your total CTC, then reviewing the offer letters and employment contracts you signed, there should be no conditions that put some restriction regarding the eligibility to get the variable pay. In case the company persists not to pay, other formalities include issuing a legal notice of the demand of the variable pay alongside showing the employment period and the companyâs legal binding to pay . If there is no positive response obtained, then the remedy of filing of complaint can be with the Labour Commissioner or Industrial Tribunal under section 15 of Payment of wages Act , 1936 that deals with the payment of wages on certain premises. For more specific advice and policy directions that may be specific to your case, it is advisable to consult a lawyer who handles employment law.Hope you find this advice beneficial.

question: Hi, I had signed a bond for 3years in company, I completed 2 years in that company, now I want to move out of that company, now they are asking me to pay the amount of bond which is 5 lakhs, Can I go legally on this, and how much time does it takes if I go legally?( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,In general rule, You will be required to reimburse the company for "liquidated damages" if you choose to leave before the agreed period. Bond agreements can be enforceable if they are designed to protect the employer's legitimate interests and are reasonable in nature. If the bond amount is unreasonable, you have the option to challenge the bond and it becomes unenforceable. You always check with your employer on what alternatives are. You can serve a notice period as per your employment contract. Try to negotiate with your employer. In case negotiation fails, you can challenge the bond before the court by giving a legal notice to the employer. The duration of the legal procedure shall depend upon the complexity of the case. We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question: School should not give 1month salary and experience certificate( Sonepat, Haryana )

question: Dear sir, I had left my previous company on August 2021 its been 3 years, after that i join 2 more company but they dont have PF service even my current company team size is less then 10 member so they also dont have PF facility, Due to urgent cash need i thought to close my PF account and withdraw the amount from EPF, when I had check my EPF accounts some random company had open my EPF,  I had no idea about this company how they had got my documents and how they have open my EPF accounts the joining date is showing 01/01/2023 and they have not marked the exit date, now i dont know what to do( Mumbai City, Maharashtra )

Explain the matter to your previous employer and your current employer about the opening of the unauthorized EPF account and the misuse of the documents. You can file a complaint before the police station regarding the fraudulent activity or you can file a complaint before the Cyber Crime cell. We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question: Hi sir/madam, my mom was the sole bread winner of our family throughout my life. I am 39yrs currently. She belongs to SC community and I have a SC caste certificate too which I utilizes to get tuition fee waiver/reduction for my MSc and PhD degrees. My dad belongs to general category, but he never had any job. I would like to apply for professor/scientist jobs in central govt research institutions (eg CSIR labs), IITs, IISERs etc. Am I eligible to use my SC certificate? Or should I apply under general category? Legally what is correct? Thank you( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,On the basis of the SC caste certificate, you can directly apply for any post of Professor or Scientist in the central government research organizations like CSIR labs, IITs and IISERs. Since your mother is from the SC community and she was the only earning member of the family you can avail the privileges accruing out of the SC status even if your father belongs to general caste. Furthermore, there is the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Reservation in Posts and Services) Act 1993 to back up the policy concerning the reservation of the government jobs for the candidates belonging to the SC/ST category. Make sure that your SC caste certificate is in order as it may be required to produce it during the period of recruitment. As for the hiring criteria, you need to check in the relevant job announcements since they may differ depending on the private or public institution. Application under the SC category would mean you fall under it thus be entitled to any reservation or relaxations as to the requirements.Hope you found this advice fruitful.

question: Hi, I have been working in my company for 4 years and I have not received my June 2024 salary. They are constantly giving an excuse that cash flow is less so salary is pending while all other employees except me have received the salary. Please tell me what should I do now. I mailed and requested them multiple times but nothing worked( Kolkata, West Bengal )

question: whether I am eligible for Higher Pension?( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,EPFO issued a circular in December 2022 providing the eligibility criteria and application process for claiming a higher pension. The criteria's are- the employees retired before 01/09/2014. The employees exercised the joint option under para 11(3) of EPS-95 while being a member of EPS-95. The employees and employers contributed EPS on salaries exceeding the wage ceiling of Rs.5,000 or Rs.6,500. However, the EPFO circular did not provide a higher pension option for employees who were part of the EPF before 01/09/2014 but still working/retired after 2014. As per the Supreme Court judgement, such employees were also eligible to claim a higher pension. EPFO issued another circular mentioning higher pension eligibility criteria for employees in service/retired after 2014. Eligibility criteria to file a joint option for getting a higher pension: The employees who were members before 01/09/2014 continued to be members after that date. The employees and employers contributed to EPS on salaries exceeding the wage ceiling of Rs.5,000 or Rs.6,500. The employees and employers were members of EPS-95 and did not exercise the joint option provided under the deleted para 11(3) of the EPS and amendment of 2014. If you fulfill the eligibility criteria, you are eligible for Higher Pension. We hope that our response is helpful to you.

question:
Sir currently l am doing a govt job and also have been selected on another govt job. I Joined the 2nd govt job but due to  grevious medical problems at my home l submitted representation within one week regarding withdrawal of joining. And after another week l submitted another representation regarding seeking extension or 2nd chance of joining. 
Now in view of above , will l be able to get the same.( Kolkata, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,As per law, an employee cannot rejoin the same job ,once the resignation is accepted, because when the resignation is accepted , then there is no relation between employee and employer. The general rule is for rejoining the central government service is that the employee should have left the job in a proper and valid manner. This means that the employee should have completed their notice period and obtained a relieving letter from their previous employer. If the gap is less than three years, the employee can rejoin the government service in the same or a lower position as per their previous designation. The employee will also be entitled to the same pay scale and benefits as they were receiving before they left the job. But withdrawal of joining and resignation are not same. The extension or second chance of joining, depends on the policy of the government department. The policy lays down the conditions for granting extension. If you have submitted all the evidences of your grievous medical problems at home, it might strengthen your representation. Contact the HR department of the government department, submit all the relevant documents and medical certificate and request for extension. Your request might get granted. We hope our response is helpful to you.

question:
Is there any court judgment that clarifies the clause 'should have' and 'must have'.

For reference there is judgment in similar matter in the case of RAJBEER SINGH VS STATE OF PUNJAB '
where court has said that 'should have' is directory whereas 'must have' is mandatory.( Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,In an order of judgment, the use of words or terms "should have" and "might have" is sequential and circumstantial to define and clarify its enforceability in terms of the specific statute applicable in a suit or dispute. In English grammar, shall is one of the âmodal verbsâ (also known as âhelping verbsâ) like can, will, could, shall, must, would, might, and should. The purpose of a modal verb is to add meaning to the main verb in a sentence by expressing possibility, ability, permission, or obligation. The most common ones are shall, will, may, should, would and might. âShallâ or "should" is a word of command that imposes a duty or obligation. It requires a specific action to be taken and does not leave room for discretion. âMayâ or "might" in legal terms grants the permission or discretion to act in a certain way, but it is not mandatory. Gives an option for something, that does require it. It is important to distinguish between âmayâ and âshallâ in legal documents, as they convey different meanings. âMayâ indicates permissibility, while âshallâ denotes obligation. Hope your query stands clarified.

question:
I am writing to bring to your attention an unauthorized deduction from my Provident Fund (PF) account. Upon reviewing my latest pay slip for May 2024, I noticed that an advance had been deducted without my prior knowledge or consent.            With reference to my pay slip for May 2024, I observed a deduction of Rs. 1,76,400.00 from my Provident Fund account and Rs. 4900.00 from my salary. I have not applied for any advance or loan from my PF account, and I am deeply concerned about this unauthorized transaction.
             On 05.06.2024, I sent an email to the Airport Director regarding the unauthorized transaction, but I did not receive any reply until 17.06.2024. Consequently, I sent a reminder email on 18.06.2024 (after 14 days), but there was still no response. I contacted the Grievance Officer through phone on 19.06.2024, and as a result, on 20.06.2024 at 07:13 AM, the officer responsible for the unauthorized deduction contacted me via phone. He pressured me to accept the amount in my bank account and repay it as a PF advance, but I did not agree and requested that the amount be reversed to my CPF account to avoid any financial loss. Subsequently, at 09:36 AM, I received an email stating that I had agreed to receive the amount in my bank account and settle it as a PF advance. This claim is false.
              On 30.05.2024, I requested a tour advance in reference to the tour order No. AA/CL/TOUR/HR/1154-1161 dated 29.05.2024, and also intimated the unauthorized deduction. The officer accepted his mistake. On 03.06.2024, I contacted him to inquire about the status, and he informed me that he would collect another application for PF advance from the one who is applied for PF Advance and credit the amount to my bank account. I did not agree and requested that he close the PF advance with that amount. Hearing this, he disconnected the call. Therefore, on 05.06.2024, I sent an email to the Airport Director regarding the unauthorized transaction and awaited a favourable reply but, unfortunately, received none.
                  On 10.06.2024 and 11.06.2024, I tried contacting  AGM (Finance), on his personal mobile and official landline (ext. 416) multiple times, but he did not attend my calls. I called the finance section, collected the HOD (Finance) number (ext. 405), and confirmed that both the HOD and AGM(Fin) were present in their seats. However, neither HOD(Fin) nor AGM (Fin)  attended my calls. Since I did not agree with his proposal, he purposefully delayed or possibly denied my tour advance until 11.06.2024 (applied on 30.05.2024).
                    I feel that because I am a non-executive / C-level employee, the Airport Director, Finance HOD, and AGM (Finance) have neither acknowledged nor provided a favourable solution to this serious issue till date.
     kindly provide a legal advice in this regard as there is no response since 04.06.2024( Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,In your situation, it is crucial to address the unauthorized deduction from your Provident Fund (PF) account legally and formally. You have already taken several steps, including notifying the relevant authorities and following up through emails and phone calls. Since there has been no satisfactory response, you can take the following actions:Formal Written Complaint: Draft a detailed formal complaint highlighting the unauthorized deduction, the lack of communication, and the undue pressure you faced. Address this complaint to the highest authority in your organization, such as the Managing Director or the Chairman, and send it via registered post or through a reliable courier service to ensure receipt.Lodge a Grievance with EPFO: If your organization is registered with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), you can lodge a grievance through the EPFO's online portal. Provide all relevant details and documentation to support your claim.Legal Notice: Engage a lawyer to send a legal notice to the concerned parties in your organization, demanding the reversal of the unauthorized deduction and compensation for any financial loss incurred due to the delay.Labour Commissioner: You can file a complaint with the Labour Commissionerâs office, as unauthorized deductions and non-response to legitimate queries fall under unfair labor practices. The Labour Commissioner can intervene and mediate in such disputes.RTI Application: If your organization is a government or semi-government entity, file a Right to Information (RTI) application seeking details about the unauthorized deduction, the actions taken on your complaint, and the reasons for the delay in addressing your grievance.File a Police Complaint: In extreme cases, if the unauthorized deduction persists and you face continued harassment, you can file a police complaint for fraud and misappropriation of funds.These steps should compel the authorities to take your complaint seriously and provide a prompt resolution. Make sure to keep records of all communications and responses for future reference.Thank You

question:
Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, joint representation by  government servants on matters of common interest is prohibited. 

Could you please clarify how has the term 'representation'. been officially defined? Can any communication even if it is not concerned with service matters be called representation or only those communications which pertain only to service related matters and any claim, demand, complain, or grievance in respect thereof are representations.( Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,As per DOPT OM No. 11013/11/97-Estt.(A), dated 06.11.1997 The representations from Government servants on service matters are broadly classified as follows - (1) Representations/complaints regarding non-payment of salary/allowances or other dues; (2) Representations on other service matters; (3) Representations against the orders of the immediate superior authority; and (4) Appeals and petitions under statutory rules and orders (e.g. Classification, Control and Appeal Rules and the petition Instructions). Any representation other than these classified representations if made by a public servant without proper channels i.e, routed through HOD is considered a violation of Rule 20 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964. Hope the matter stands clarified.

question: In my previous company they'll hold my FnF amount, after 5 months from resignation they released my settlement amount, but they're not credited my salary for the notice period. What can I do?( Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh )

question: I was in judicial custody on IPC 304 B. Include details of your absence due to judicial custody, the communication you had with your reporting manager, and your desire to resume work now that you are on bail.Negotiate: If the organization claims there are no vacancies or they have hired someone else for your role, try to negotiate with them for alternative positions within the company that match your skills and qualifications. Highlight your past performance and contributions to the organization to strengthen your case for reinstatement.Legal Action: If the organization refuses to reinstate you or negotiate alternative positions despite your efforts, you may consider taking legal action. Consult a lawyer specializing in labor law to assess the merits of your case and explore legal remedies such as filing a complaint with the labor department or approaching the labor court for reinstatement and compensation for wrongful termination.Document Everything: Keep records of all communication with the organization, copies of letters or emails exchanged, and any other relevant documentation that supports your claim for reinstatement.Stay Professional: Throughout the process, maintain a professional demeanor and adhere to the organization's protocols and procedures for addressing employment-related issues.

question: Sir I want to know that where should I consult to resolve the overlapping date in my PF Account . My employer is not ready to solve it from my end .( Meerut, Uttar Pradesh )

answer: Dear Client,The Company cannot force you to continue in the project unless you have signed an agreement in that regard. Rejecting the resignation letter and imposing a pre-condition to accept the same is illegal and accounts for unfair labor practices. According to Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, the terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels an employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them from joining the competitor or other employer are void to that extent. It also includes non-compete clauses, which limit the person's ability to choose their field of work. So, in this situation, if you are covered under the definition of workmen in Section 2(s) of the I D Act, then you can file a complaint to the State Labour Commissioner for unfair labor practice. But, if you hold the position of a Manager/Supervisor in the company, you have to file a suit before the jurisdictional court and seek appropriate remedy. If required, you can consult an advocate for advice and assistance in the matter.Hope it helps.Thank you.

answer: Dear Client,Interview, selection, appointment, promotion etc all these activities were carried on by respective establishments as per the well-established recruitment policy made out considering a variety of factors and following the principle of natural justice. question: I have been asked to leave the company with serving notice period as they are closing the business unit, I have not been provided any severance package, also my ESOP which will vest in one month from the date of my last working day they are not providing me the option of using it too.( Mumbai, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Apart from compliance with the statutory formalities required under the Companies Act, 2013 for the closer of the business of a company or part of it, the Company has to comply with the statutory provisions of Labour laws before the closure of the company or a part of it.  According to Section 2(cc) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, Closure means the permanent closing down of a place of employment or part thereof. The employer must follow a specific process outlined in the law when closing the establishment. If an employer plans to close their establishment, they must apply at least ninety days in advance where the number of workmen is more than 100 to the appropriate government.(Labour Commissioner) seeking permission for closure endorsing a copy of the said application to the workersâ representatives. Section 25(O) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 allows the closure of a business without prior permission of the appropriate authority if it has less than 50 workers and compensates the workers with 15 daysâ average pay for each completed year of service as severance package. The employer must notify the government authority and workers at least 60 days in advance or provide wages instead of notice and pay the compensation at the time of closure or within 15 days from the notice, whichever comes first. An employer with more than 50 workers must apply for prior permission of the appropriate government before the closure of their establishment under Section 25(N) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. Itâs crucial to understand that the term âworkmenâ includes not only permanent employees but also contractual, casual and temporary workers who have worked for more than one year in the establishment. An illegal closure occurs when an employer shuts down an establishment without following procedures outlined in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. This is a serious violation with legal consequences. Workmen affected by an illegal closure are entitled to reinstatement with full back wages once they raise an Industrial dispute before the Industrial Tribunal or Labour Court. So, in the given situation, if you are aggrieved with the severance package offered or denied by the Company on the closure of the business, you can escalate your grievance before the concerned Labour Commission and can file an application under Sec.33(C)(2) of the I D Act before the Labour Court/Industrial Tribunal claiming the dues payable by the company on the closure of the business. Feel free to contact our legal team to navigate the issue in the right way.

A joint declaration form(JDF) is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. An EPF member should fill out the joint declaration form(JDF) with correct details like fatherâs name, joining date, Exit date, etc., as these details will be verified with the Aadhaar. The EPF member or employee should submit the joint declaration form countersigned by the concerned employer who entered the wrong data by mistake to the regional PF office with which the company or establishment is registered. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database of EPF Account, he/she should contact present or previous employers and get it corrected. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of dual employment in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to rectify any anomaly in EPF records of a member on receipt of JDF. In case of non-cooperation from the employer, a member of the EPF Account can file a complaint against them using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). Once you succeed in wiping out the stigma of dual employment or overlapping of service from your EPF records with the cooperation of your employers, your EPF records showing the correct date of employment shall be restored.

I joined on 18th Apr and resigned on 20th April next year. But company is denying the bonus which was promised to be given post 1 year from DOJ by saying that I was on notice period when the payout was done i.e on 26th April.

Offer letter says:-
The payout will be done in the payroll cycle as per the defined timelines above, subject to you being on rolls of the company and not serving notice.

What should I do in this case ?( Patna, Bihar )
answer: Dear Client,As per the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, an employee is eligible to receive a bonus under the Act, on fulfillment of the following criteria: an employee who receives a salary/wage up to Rs. 21,000/- per month (As per Amendment of 2015) and the employee must have worked in the factory or establishment for not less than 30 days in a year(FY). Section 10 of the Act prescribes the minimum bonus(statutory bonus), that is 8.33% of the employeeâs Salary/wages, which is the least percent mandatorily to be paid by every establishment or organization covered by the Act, and as per Section 11 of the Act, the maximum amount of bonus shall not exceed, 20% of the salary/wages of the employees. For bonus calculation, only the employeeâs Salary/Wages and Dearness allowance are considered. The bonus shall be paid within 8 months from the end of the accounting year, or within a month from the date of enforcement of the Act. So, in view of the above provision of the relevant Act that has an overriding effect on any contract or agreement made contrary to the provision of the Act shall be infructuous and unenforceable and the eligible employee can claim a statutory bonus once he fulfills the eligibility criteria regardless of their terms of employment. Apparently, the actions of the Company may be treated as unfair labour practice, and accordingly, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, and apart, you should file an application u/s.33C(2) of I D Act before the concerned Labour Court claiming your unpaid bonus and other dues receivable on your resignation from the Company. But, if you are holding the position of manager or Administrative Officer in the Company, you have to file a money suit before the Civil Court for recovery of your dues from the company.

question:
I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to seek your legal advice regarding an employment matter. I have been working as a payroll contract technician in a PSU for the past 12 years, with my contract being extended on a yearly basis. However, I have recently been informed that my contract will terminate in September 2024, as per the decision of the management.

I joined the company in 2011, and in 2016, the company started recruiting employees on a tenure basis. These employees receive permanent employee salaries, allowances, and promotions. I have not received such benefits despite my long-standing service with the company.

I seek your advice on whether there is any legal recourse available to me for regularization or for receiving salaries and allowances equivalent to tenure employees. I would greatly appreciate it if you could provide me with your expert opinion on this matter.( Palakkad, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,Usually, PSUs enter into agreements with outsourcing agencies that provide manpower for a particular project or for general day-to-day work in a particular department. PSUs go for outsourcing when it does not have sufficient regular manpower or for eg, a new project is there for a particular duration of time. A contractual employee of PSU can't be permanent. To get appointed as a permanent Government employee, he/she has to clear a competitive examination as per recruitment rules. Outsourcing is generally done on a permanent basis. Subcontracting is generally done on a temporary basis. On the other hand, the Contract Labour [Regulation and Abolition] Act, 1970 is enacted to regulate the proper operation of contract workers and prevent their exploitation at the hands of management. Under Section 10(2)(b) of the Contract Labour(R & A) Act, 1970, the engagement of contract labour in permanent and perennial jobs is prohibited and violation of this provision shall cause an employer to face legal consequences including regularisation of the contractual employee. Recently, the Supreme Court ruled out in the case of Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. v. Brajrajnagar Coal Mines Workersâ Union, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 270, decided on 12-03-2024, that the workers employed to perform perennial/permanent nature of work couldn't be treated as contract workers under the Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970 to deny them the benefit of regularization of a job. Given the above proposition of relevant law and the decision of the Apex Court, when you have been working in a position on continuous renewal of the annual contract for the last 12 years in a PSU, the nature of the job itself proves that you were engaged continuously in a permanent and perennial job/vacancy in the establishment and accordingly in view of the provision of  Section 10(2)(b) of the Contract Labour(R & A) Act, 1970, you can claim your regularisation in the job filing an application before the appropriate authority constituted under the Act, i.e, the State Labour Commissioner who is empowered under Sec.10 of the Industrial Dispute Act to refer an industrial dispute to the Industrial Tribunal for adjudication, failing which you can approach the High Court seeking review of the order of the appropriate authority and for an order of adjudication of the dispute. Reach out to an Advocate handling service and labour Court matters for guidance and steps. Feel free to contact our legal team to avail of our expert service to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: I resigned job in my previous company, I worked in there 6 months and they deducted my 15 days salary. answer: Dear Client,Apparently, it is an exemplary example of unfair labour practice, many employers adopted to deprive an employee of his legitimate claim or service-linked benefits across the country. In the absence of a contract of employment, there exists no relationship between the employer and the employee and the employer takes the opportunity to exploit the career of an employee. However, such an unfair practice can be challenged if the employee provides sufficient evidence and proof of his engagement or employment in an establishment. A few pieces of evidence like salary slips, bank statements showing the credit of monthly salary, deduction EPF or ESI contribution etc can prove your claim well before the Authority or Court. So, in the given situation, serving a legal notice to the employer/company, and filing a complaint before the State Labour Commissioner can resolve the dispute provided you are a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the I D Act. Additionally, you can file an application before the State Labour Court under Sec.33C(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 claiming your dues(15 days short payment) from the company. Otherwise, if you were holding the position of Manager or Administrative Officer in the company then you have to file a civil suit against the company for recovery of your dues.

answer: Dear Client,The Company is not allowed to withhold your Full and Final Settlement amount after the resignation. However, they can deduct an amount proportional to the unfulfilled portion of the notice period from the FNF settlement amount. So, ensure that you have served the notice period before taking any legal actions. In this case, to address the default, you can send a legal notice to the company and demand for the recovery of settlement amount. You can also file a complaint before the State Labour Commissioner regarding the unpaid settlement dues. Further, if your concerns are not addressed, you can file a suit against the employer before the Labour Court under Section 33C(2) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 (ID Act) and seek for the recovery of the amount. If you are not covered under the definition of workmen in Section 2(s) of the I D Act, then you can file a civil suit. You can file a case before the jurisdictional civil court under Order 37 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 and seek for the FNF settlement. If required, you can consult an advocate for advice and compliance.Hope it helps.Thank you.

question: Nowadays, there are no rules protecting employees from layoffs, regardless of whether they are contractual or permanent. It seems that most IT companies have adopted a strategy under the guise of performance. From my personal experience, even if an employee performs well and contributes significantly, if the company finds that they can hire a cheaper candidate and save on salary costs, they will do so. They force the employee who earns a higher salary to train someone with a lower salary. Once the knowledge transfer (KT) is complete, if the lower-paid individual is capable, the company will dismiss the higher-paid employee citing performance issues. They do not consider the impact on the employeeâs family, their expenses, rent, or how they will manage daily life and repay loans. In these situations, the affected employee is left speechless and disillusioned. Consequently, IT employees are forced to take on contractual jobs alongside permanent positions to ensure some job security. However, if they are terminated from one job without notice, they might seek another contractual job. But if the contractual job also deducts Provident Fund for two or three months, PF contributions overlap, and eventually, the employee becomes jobless. This scenario explains why skilled employees are becoming jobless. Please help, what should we do if an employer fires an employee in such cases?( East Delhi, Delhi )

Duties of conciliation officers.- (relevant section 12(2) of ID Act)(1) Where any industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, the conciliation officer may, or where the dispute relates to a public utility service and a notice under section 22 has been given, shall hold conciliation proceedings in the prescribed manner.(2) The conciliation officer shall, for the purpose of bringing about a settlement of the dispute, without delay, investigate the dispute and all matters affecting the merits and the right settlement thereof and may do all such things as he thinks fit for the purpose of inducing the parties to come to a fair and amicable settlement of the dispute.(3) If a settlement of the dispute or of any of the matters in dispute is arrived at in the course of the conciliation proceedings the conciliationofficer shall send a report thereof to the appropriate Government 1 or an officer authorised in this behalf by the appropriate Government] together with a memorandum of the settlement signed by the parties to the dispute.(4) If no such settlement is arrived at, the conciliation officer shall, as soon as practicable after the close of the investigation, send to the appropriate Government a full report setting forth the steps taken by him for ascertaining the facts and circumstances relating to the dispute and for bringing about a settlement thereof, together with a full statement of such facts and circumstances, and the reasons on account of which, in his opinion, a settlement could not be arrived at.(5) If, on a consideration of the report referred to in sub- section (4), the appropriate Government is satisfied that there is a case for reference to a Board, 2 Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal,] it may make such reference. question: I have worked in a software services firm for 9 years in Pune. My last working day was 9th Dec 2023 and the employer has still not released the gratuity cheque. They are not even providing an ETA and have stopped responding to my emails.( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,With the enactment of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, gratuity payment has become mandatory for the establishment where it is applicable. A gratuity must be paid to an employee upon cessation of employment if he or she has rendered continuous service for five years or more, according to Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act of 1972. Section 4(2) of the Act provides that for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of 6 months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the prescribed rates. According to section 2A of the Act, an employee is said to be in continuous service for a period if he has for that period been in uninterrupted service including service which may be interrupted on account of accident, sickness, leave, absence from duty without leave, layoff, strike or a lock-out or cessation of work not due to any fault of employee. In view of the above proposition of law, when you rendered uninterrupted and continuous service for 9 years in an establishment, you are eligible for payment of gratuity payable by your employer as per the provision of the Payment of Gratuity Act. The Gratuity Benefits are calculated using the following formula:-(15/26) multiplied by (No of Completed Years on Exit) multiplied by (Terminal Wages/Salary). Under Rule 7(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Rules, 1972, an employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Act, or any person authorized, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, within thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form 'I' to the employer who is duty bound to disburse the gratuity within 30 days of cessation of employment of employee or claim made by an employee. After the completion of 30 days, the employer has to pay you not only the gratuity amount but also the simple interest accrued for the delay in payment of the gratuity. In case of denial of gratuity by the employer, reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner and the Controlling Authority under the Act to file a complaint against the employer over non-payment of gratuity. As regards non-payment of ETA, you need to file an application under Sec.33C(2) of the I D Act against the Company before the State Labour Court claiming recovery of entire dues receivable to an ex-employee.
